findings.finding_value: Reading T5 as a whole reveals mercy's formative character: it is not static but inherently developmental and generative. The T5 synthesis: mercy produces dual transformation (objective condition + subjective orientation simultaneously); it moves persons through named inner-state sequences (at least four distinct sequences, Q&A-128); its mechanism is always specific, embodied, and costly; suffering is both the context that generates mercy-seeking and the formation-medium through which mercy-capacity deepens (Q&A-135); mercy functions as the first and foundational inner garment in the character formation sequence (Q&A-138); and mercy has an eschatological trajectory (future fullness in which the mercy-relationship is complete and permanent). T5.7 closed (no constitutional body deposit). The overarching T5 finding: mercy is a characteristic that is received, then forms the person into one who can receive it more deeply and extend it more genuinely — it has an inherent developmental arc.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional architecture (spirit-soul interface origin, soul-level operation, embodied expression) maps directly onto T5's formative sequences (the four inner-state sequences in Q&A-128 all show external mercy entering through the soul level and producing inner-state transformation). The receiving-before-generating origin (T2) means the formative developmental arc (T5) always begins with external mercy received, not internal mercy generated.

findings.finding_value: T4's relational chain (God→human→human mercy) and T5's formative arc (mercy received forms mercy-giving capacity) are structurally identical processes described at different levels. findings.finding_value: T5 as a whole establishes contrition's formative logic: it is a threshold event that is not an end-state but a passage. The sequence (crushing → contrite posture → divine reviving → restored inner being) shows that the formation contrition produces is not the settling into permanent brokenness but the emergence of a character shaped by repeated breaking-and-reviving. The mechanism is dissolution-through-encounter — the inner being's self-protective structures dissolved by a reality it cannot absorb without being changed. Contrition functions as the recurring inner reset in the sanctification arc, preventing the accumulation of pride and self-sufficiency. T5.7 closes formally (no body deposit), which confirms that contrition's formative work is entirely inner-constitutional, not somatic-residual. The eschatological trajectory (T5.6) points forward but is underdeveloped in the verse evidence — the data indicates contrition is oriented toward joy and revival but does not name a final eschatological fullness.

findings.finding_value: The definition tier (T1) positions contrition as a threshold event (not an end-state but a passage toward divine response); the formative tier (T5) confirms and extends this by showing that contrition's productive function is precisely its threshold character — it is the recurring event through which the person is returned to receptivity. T1's sequence (crushing → contrite posture → divine response) maps directly onto T5's formative arc (dissolution-through-encounter → contrite state → character of lowliness formed through repeated cycles). The definitional claim that contrition is a passage rather than a terminal state (T1) is confirmed by T5's formation account: the sustainable inner posture produced is not permanent brokenness but the characterological lowliness that emerges from repeated breaking-and-reviving.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-023: The relational tier (T4) establishes that contrition creates the condition for divine-human relational proximity; the formative tier (T5) shows that this relational positioning is the goal of contriti…
findings.finding_value: The relational tier (T4) establishes that contrition creates the condition for divine-human relational proximity; the formative tier (T5) shows that this relational positioning is the goal of contrition's formative work. Together T4 and T5 reveal that contrition's formation is relational formation — the character produced by repeated contrition is not moral character in the abstract but the specific relational disposition of creaturely proximity to God. The settled lowliness produced by T5 is precisely the inner posture that T4 names as the condition for divine dwelling and divine looking. Formation (T5) and relational positioning (T4) are therefore the same reality described longitudinally and synchronically: T5 shows the character being formed; T4 shows what that character makes possible.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-026: The formative tier (T5) shows that contrition's formation produces the settled lowliness and word-permeability that Isa 66:2 designates; the structural relationships tier (T6) shows that contrition is…
findings.finding_value: The formative tier (T5) shows that contrition's formation produces the settled lowliness and word-permeability that Isa 66:2 designates; the structural relationships tier (T6) shows that contrition is constitutive of genuine repentance (T6.3). Together T5 and T6 reveal the inner logic of contrition's formative productivity: contrition forms the character that makes genuine repentance possible (T6.3 constitutive relationship) and sustains the inner posture (lowliness, word-permeability) that the structural connections (fear, heart) express in their own vocabularies. The formation account (T5) explains why contrition has such dense structural connections (T6) — it is the inner-being event that produces the character from which the connected characteristics flow.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-027: The formative tier (T5) identifies the sequence and mechanism of contrition's development; the evidential tier (T7) provides the verse base from which these are derived. The sequence (crushing → contr…
findings.finding_value: The formative tier (T5) identifies the sequence and mechanism of contrition's development; the evidential tier (T7) provides the verse base from which these are derived. The sequence (crushing → contrite posture → divine reviving, T5.2) is derivable from the primary anchor verses (T7.2): Psa 51's progression, Isa 57:15's three-movement structure, Psa 34:18's bicolon. The dissolution-through-encounter mechanism (T5.3) is most clearly grounded in Isa 57:15 as the primary anchor (T7.2.5). T5's formative account is not speculative but exegetically derived: T7 provides the textual ground; T5 provides the formative interpretation. The highest-evidenced formative movement (the crushing-to-reviving sequence) is precisely the movement most clearly encoded in the primary anchor verses.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — a formation sequence: (1) Volitional alignment / self-joining (Psa 119:63, Phili 3:10 — initiating acts); (2) Habitual participation (sustained fellowship over time); (3) Constitutional formation (Jer 13:23 — fixed character as the endpoint). For divine nature participation (2Pe 1:4): (1) Receipt of divine promise; (2) Escape from corrupting desire; (3) Participation in divine nature. OBS-062-048, OBS-062-052, OBS-062-058.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-062-005: T5 establishes fellowship as the primary relational mechanism of sanctification in this registry — character is formed not through solitary disciplines but through participatory community alignment. T…
findings.finding_value: T5 establishes fellowship as the primary relational mechanism of sanctification in this registry — character is formed not through solitary disciplines but through participatory community alignment. The formation sequence (volitional alignment → habitual participation → constitutional fixing) runs from free choice to constrained character, meaning the initial choice of fellowship objects is made at maximum freedom and progressively constrains freedom as character forms. Two distinct formative mechanisms operate: participatory transfer (habituation producing conformity — gradual) and wound-as-cleansing (somatic event producing inner purification — acute). The eschatological trajectory (T5.6) is explicit in 2Pe 1:4 — fellowship is oriented toward divine nature participation as its telos.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-011: T1 establishes that habitual fellowship produces constitutional character formation; T5 maps this as the primary formation mechanism and identifies the sequence (volitional alignment → habituation → c…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes that habitual fellowship produces constitutional character formation; T5 maps this as the primary formation mechanism and identifies the sequence (volitional alignment → habituation → constitutional fixing). Together T1 and T5 reveal the full arc: the definitional claim that fellowship's object determines character (T1) is the endpoint of a formation process that moves through distinct phases (T5). The five-mode structure (T1) generates two distinct formation mechanisms in T5: participatory-transfer (companionship → habituation → character) and wound-as-cleansing (suffering → inner purification). T1's most radical mode (ontological, 2Pe 1:4) is T5's eschatological telos (divine nature participation as the formation endpoint).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-016: T2's constitutional map and T5's formative account describe the same reality from space and time perspectives. The desire-faculty (T2.5) as constitutional engine maps onto T5's formation sequence begi…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional map and T5's formative account describe the same reality from space and time perspectives. The desire-faculty (T2.5) as constitutional engine maps onto T5's formation sequence beginning point (volitional alignment — desire-directed). The heart-level formation (T2.3 — Psa 119:63, Jer 13:23) is T5's constitutional-formation endpoint. The body-deposit question (T2.8) opens into T5.7's developmental consequence analysis — the wound-mark as a formative trace raises the question of whether suffering-fellowship leaves a permanent constitutional marker, a question that remains open pending Session D.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-020: T3's snapshot (what fellowship does to faculties in the moment) and T5's longitudinal account (what habitual fellowship produces over time) together reveal that faculty deepening (T3) is the process o…
findings.finding_value: T3's snapshot (what fellowship does to faculties in the moment) and T5's longitudinal account (what habitual fellowship produces over time) together reveal that faculty deepening (T3) is the process of which constitutional character formation (T5) is the endpoint. The right-direction faculty deepening (T3 — perception, cognition, conscience, moral evaluation each deepened by right fellowship) accumulates over time into the fixed character of Psa 119:63's declared God-fearer companion, which is on its way to Jer 13:23's constitutional formation. T3 → T5 is the moment-to-character arc.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-023: T4's relational architecture (vertical primary; horizontal derived) and T5's formation arc (habituation → constitutional character) are structurally connected through 1Jo 1:3: the horizontal fellowshi…
findings.finding_value: T4's relational architecture (vertical primary; horizontal derived) and T5's formation arc (habituation → constitutional character) are structurally connected through 1Jo 1:3: the horizontal fellowship is derived from and grounded in the vertical (T4), and the vertical fellowship is the source from which the horizontal formation extends (T5 — the person who has received divine fellowship can extend human fellowship that is grounded in that divine reality). T4's scope-narrows-as-depth-increases finding is T5's formation telos: the deepest fellowship (divine nature participation — 2Pe 1:4) is also the narrowest in scope and the furthest eschatological endpoint.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-026: T5's formation mechanisms (participatory transfer and wound-as-cleansing) explain why fellowship is structurally connected in T6 to both desire (R43 — participatory-transfer mechanism begins with desi…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation mechanisms (participatory transfer and wound-as-cleansing) explain why fellowship is structurally connected in T6 to both desire (R43 — participatory-transfer mechanism begins with desire-directed alignment) and to contrition/sorrow (R30, R151 — wound-as-cleansing mechanism meets contrition and sorrow at Isa 53:5). T5's two formation mechanisms generate two distinct clusters of T6 structural connections: the habitual-alignment cluster (R43 desire, R167 unity, R34 covenant) and the suffering-cleansing cluster (R30 contrition, R151 sorrow, R192 comfort). Formation mechanism determines structural cluster.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-062-027: T5's formation sequence (volitional alignment → habituation → constitutional fixing) is grounded in T7's verse evidence. The sequence beginning point (volitional alignment) is carried by Psa 119:63 (w…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation sequence (volitional alignment → habituation → constitutional fixing) is grounded in T7's verse evidence. The sequence beginning point (volitional alignment) is carried by Psa 119:63 (wisdom poetry — declared dispositional alignment). The habituation arc is carried by the prophetic diagnostic setting (Jer 13:23, Hos 4:17 — naming the fixed endpoint of wrong habitual fellowship). The constitutional telos (divine nature participation) is carried by the apostolic-theological setting (2Pe 1:4). T7's literary forms track the formation sequence from beginning (wisdom poetry) through middle (prophetic diagnosis) to eschatological telos (apostolic theology).

findings.session_b_note: Sequence: (1) Offence/guilt present (prior condition); (2) Access-posture adopted (faith, repentance, confession — reception-preparation); (3) Forgiveness received (status-change); (4) Love-response generated (Luk 7:47); (5) Capacity to extend forgiveness formed (Mat 18:35 structural logic); (6) Extended forgiveness to others (horizontal expression). For the new covenant: steps 3 and 4 produce permanent new conditions (Jer 31:34 — known by God, sins remembered no more). OBS-064-017, OBS-064-022, OBS-064-029, OBS-064-032.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-064-005: T5 establishes forgiveness as a transitional-formative characteristic: it transforms condition (guilt-bearing → guilt-freed) and orientation (toward love-production and reverence-formation) but does n…
findings.finding_value: T5 establishes forgiveness as a transitional-formative characteristic: it transforms condition (guilt-bearing → guilt-freed) and orientation (toward love-production and reverence-formation) but does not leave a constitutional body deposit (T5.7 closed). The formation sequence is specific (offence → access-posture → forgiveness received → love generated → capacity to extend → horizontal extension) and the eschatological endpoint is identified (Jer 31:34 — permanent new covenant forgiveness as the telos). Two formation mechanisms (declaratory and atoning) operate at different levels but combine in the NT's atonement-grounded declaratory forgiveness. The suffering cost on the forgiver's side (Eph 1:7 — "through his blood"; absorbed wrong in horizontal forgiveness) is structurally necessary. T5.7 closes: forgiveness leaves no constitutional body deposit, which means the formative work is entirely inner-constitutional. The eschatological dimension is strong: Jer 31:34 provides the telos (permanent sins-remembered-no-more) toward which all present forgiveness-acts point.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-011: T1 establishes forgiveness as transitional (not terminal); T5 confirms this and maps the formation arc. T1's downstream states (love, reverence) are T5's immediate formation products. T1's sustained c…
findings.finding_value: T1 establishes forgiveness as transitional (not terminal); T5 confirms this and maps the formation arc. T1's downstream states (love, reverence) are T5's immediate formation products. T1's sustained conditions (freed access to God, enabled worship, capacity to extend) are T5's longer-arc formation outcomes. T1's eschatological orientation (Jer 31:34 as the forward-pointing fullness) is T5's eschatological telos. The two mechanisms in T5 (declaratory and atoning) correspond to T1's two primary mode-types: the divine relational-personal mode operates through the declaratory-atoning mechanism; the human horizontal mode operates through the heart-level-release mechanism. T1 and T5 together reveal the complete arc from definition to formation endpoint.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-016: T2's constitutional movement (guilt-bearing → forgiveness → love → capacity to extend) is T5's formation sequence described at the constitutional level. T2's finding that the constitutional event prod…
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional movement (guilt-bearing → forgiveness → love → capacity to extend) is T5's formation sequence described at the constitutional level. T2's finding that the constitutional event produces further inner states (love, direct access to God) is T5's transitional-formative account. The body-deposit gap (T2.8 — data silent; T5.7 closed) means the formation is entirely inner-constitutional — the formative event leaves no somatic residue, which is consistent with T5's finding that forgiveness is transitional rather than permanently marking. The eschatological telos (T5.6 — Jer 31:34) is the permanent constitutional state that present forgiveness-events anticipate.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-020: T3's faculty deepenings (cognition enabled — Jer 31:34; love produced — Luk 7:47; conscience purified — Heb 9:14; volition redirected) are T5's formation products described at the faculty level. The f…
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty deepenings (cognition enabled — Jer 31:34; love produced — Luk 7:47; conscience purified — Heb 9:14; volition redirected) are T5's formation products described at the faculty level. The formation sequence (T5) is the longitudinal account of which T3's faculty engagements are the synchronic snapshots. The commanded forgiveness as sanctification discipline (T5.5 — Eph 4:32) is the formation vehicle through which the volitional faculty (T3.6) is habituated and the moral evaluation faculty (T3.8) is deepened. T3 and T5 together reveal the full formation arc: T3 shows what happens to each faculty in the moment of forgiveness; T5 shows what sustained habitual forgiveness does to the person over time.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-023: T4's vertical-horizontal interdependence (the structural claim that receiving divine forgiveness enables extending human forgiveness) is T5's formation arc described at the relational level. The forma…
findings.finding_value: T4's vertical-horizontal interdependence (the structural claim that receiving divine forgiveness enables extending human forgiveness) is T5's formation arc described at the relational level. The formation sequence (T5 — forgiveness received → love generated → capacity to extend formed) is the inner development through which T4's structural interdependence is created: the person who genuinely receives divine forgiveness and generates the love-response (T5) is the person who has the genuine volitional capacity to extend horizontal forgiveness (T4). The eschatological telos (T5.6 — Jer 31:34) is also T4's permanent relational state: the guilt-barrier permanently removed produces permanently restored relational access to God.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-026: T5's formation sequence (forgiveness received → love → capacity to extend) explains why T6 finds love-103 as a co-occurrence signal (8 shared verses) — love is the formation product most visibly evide…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation sequence (forgiveness received → love → capacity to extend) explains why T6 finds love-103 as a co-occurrence signal (8 shared verses) — love is the formation product most visibly evidenced in the co-occurrence data. T5's two mechanisms (declaratory and atoning) explain the guilt-073 co-occurrence dominance (51 shared verses) — guilt is the condition both mechanisms address, and so it co-occurs across the entire forgiveness corpus. T5's sanctification-formation dimension (T5.5 — Eph 4:32) explains the reconciliation-130 shared anchor (Mat 5:24): the commanded forgiveness in the formation context is structurally connected to the restored relational state (reconciliation) as the goal of the horizontal act. T5's formation mechanisms generate T6's structural connections.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-064-027: T5's formation sequence is grounded in T7's verse evidence. The access-posture phase (T5.2 — repentance, faith, confession) is carried by the Synoptic and apostolic letter corpus (T7.2 — Act 2:38, Act…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation sequence is grounded in T7's verse evidence. The access-posture phase (T5.2 — repentance, faith, confession) is carried by the Synoptic and apostolic letter corpus (T7.2 — Act 2:38, Act 10:43, 1Jo 1:9). The forgiveness-received status change is carried by the Synoptic pronouncement corpus (Luk 7:47-48, Mar 2:5). The eschatological telos (T5.6 — Jer 31:34) is the prophetic-eschatological corpus (T7.2). T7's cross-testament vocabulary finding (NT applying divine-forgiveness vocabulary to human forgiveness — T7.1.9 and Q&A-179) is T5's formation mechanism expressed at the lexical level: the commanded human forgiveness ("as God in Christ forgave you" — Eph 4:32) is the formation vehicle, and the vocabulary is the structural carrier of the "as" claim.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-005: T5 produces three inter-related formation findings. First, transformation is evidenced in both modes simultaneously (Luke 15:20-24 — the father's compassion produces condition-change in the son's stan…
findings.finding_value: T5 produces three inter-related formation findings. First, transformation is evidenced in both modes simultaneously (Luke 15:20-24 — the father's compassion produces condition-change in the son's standing AND orientation-change in his reception of identity). Second, the formative cycle is self-reinforcing: the after-state of compassion-received feeds back into the before-state of compassion-readiness in the future — the person who has received compassion becomes more capable of extending it. Third, compassion plays a dual role in the sanctification arc: it is simultaneously the character target being formed (the person becoming compassionate over time) and the motivational ground that makes the formative relationship survivable through failure and return. Matthew 18:27 introduces the most critical formative warning: received compassion can be forfeited by failure to extend it — compassion is not a permanently possessed gift but a participatory moral framework. Three distinct mechanisms of change operate across contexts: encounter/sudden (splanchnizō — the moment of being moved), covenantal-sustaining/gradual (chesed — the steady faithfulness over time), and participatory-ontological (2Pe 1:4 pattern — sharing in what God is). T5.7 is formally closed: no body deposit established. All four relationships between suffering and compassion are evidenced — suffering reveals, tests, deepens, and produces compassion.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-023-016: T2's four-stage constitutional movement (somatic arousal → soul → volition → action) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological) ar…
findings.finding_value: T2's four-stage constitutional movement (somatic arousal → soul → volition → action) and T5's three mechanisms of change (encounter/sudden, covenantal-sustaining/gradual, participatory-ontological) are structurally complementary. T2 describes the movement within a single compassion-event; T5 describes how that event accumulates into character over time. The encounter/sudden mechanism (T5) corresponds to the full four-stage sequence of T2 in a single instance. The covenantal-sustaining mechanism (T5) corresponds to the repeated operation of the somatic-soul pathway (T2.2 — soul-level chesed as the sustaining character) over time. The participatory-ontological mechanism (T5) corresponds to the constitutional direction T2 identifies but leaves at spirit-level gap: if the deepest formation is participatory-ontological, the spirit-level dimension (T2.1 — entirely silent) may be where this operates — a convergent gap from two tiers.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-005: T5 produces the richest formation account of any characteristic in the review set. Five mechanisms of change are distinguished: encounter (specific relational event — Luk 1:28, Ruth 2:10), spirit-outp…
findings.finding_value: T5 produces the richest formation account of any characteristic in the review set. Five mechanisms of change are distinguished: encounter (specific relational event — Luk 1:28, Ruth 2:10), spirit-outpouring (Zec 12:10), word (Act 20:32 — grace operating through the proclaimed word), inference (Rom 8:32 — cognitive reasoning from the supreme grace-event to present assurance), and mediated-transformation (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving — Eph 4:32, SD030). Five distinct mechanisms for a single characteristic is unique in the programme data. The creaturely recognition response (fear → mourning → prostration) is confirmed as a consistent transitional state in all grace-sequences across different evidential contexts — not incidental detail but structural feature. Suffering's relationship to grace is precisely distinguished: grace inhabits suffering rather than suffering producing grace (2Cor 12:9 — weakness as theatre of grace, not as generator of grace). The reversibility question (T5.1 P2) is the most significant gap: not fully resolved. The eschatological trajectory (T5.6) is evidenced through Eph 2:7 ("the immeasurable riches of his grace in the coming ages") and charitoō's perfect-passive form (completed state with continuing effect). T2.8 remains open; T5.7 is formally left open accordingly.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-011: T1's sustained-effect finding (immediate/sustained contrast as qualitative, not merely temporal — what grace does immediately is creaturely recognition; what it does over time is constitution of ident…
findings.finding_value: T1's sustained-effect finding (immediate/sustained contrast as qualitative, not merely temporal — what grace does immediately is creaturely recognition; what it does over time is constitution of identity and character) maps onto T5's formation mechanisms. The encounter mechanism (T5) produces the immediate effects named in T1.5; the word, inference, and mediated-transformation mechanisms (T5) produce the sustained effects of T1.6. T5's five mechanisms collectively explain how the four kinds named in T1.2 are produced across different temporal and contextual registers: disposition-receipt is the encounter mechanism; standing is the spirit-outpouring mechanism; capacity is the mediated-transformation mechanism; character quality is the sustained word-and-inference mechanism. T1 names what is produced; T5 names how each kind is produced.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-020: T3's faculty findings are the synchronic expression of T5's diachronic formation arc. The creaturely recognition response (T5.2 — fear → mourning → prostration as the consistent transitional state in …
findings.finding_value: T3's faculty findings are the synchronic expression of T5's diachronic formation arc. The creaturely recognition response (T5.2 — fear → mourning → prostration as the consistent transitional state in all grace-sequences) is the affective-faculty event (T3.4) at the moment of grace-arrival, which then constitutes the volitional-faculty alignment (T3.6 — the agency-constituting paradox) that enables the conscientious expression (T3.10). T5's formation arc (sustained work producing character-quality) is the longitudinal development of T3.9's finding (conscience operating fully within grace) into T3.10's finding (conscientiousness as the integrated moral character that grace constitutes over time). The person who has been formed by grace through the T5 formation arc is the person in whom T3's faculty engagements have been progressively deepened and integrated.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-026: T5's five formation mechanisms explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence and sequential landscape. The encounter mechanism (sudden grace-event) corresponds to the sequences confirme…
findings.finding_value: T5's five formation mechanisms explain the structural pattern visible in T6's co-occurrence and sequential landscape. The encounter mechanism (sudden grace-event) corresponds to the sequences confirmed in T6.2 (grace precedes and causes the immediate responses of mourning, fear, supplication — SD038, SD026). The word mechanism (Act 20:32) corresponds to the faith co-occurrence (R059 — 10 verses): the proclaimed word that carries grace produces faith as its response. The inference mechanism (Rom 8:32 — assurance derived by reasoning) corresponds to the hope and peace co-occurrences (R117 — 10 verses): reasoned assurance from grace produces the inner peace and hope co-occurring registries name. The mediated-transformation mechanism (tenderheartedness → forgiving) produces the love co-occurrence (R103 — 14 verses) as tenderheartedness is the inner precondition of the forgiving that love and grace share. T5's mechanisms generate T6's structural connections.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — the new covenant evidence provides the clearest sequence in the registry. The sequence from Jer 31:31-34 / Heb 8:8-10 is: (1) Identification of failure under the old covenant — "they did not continue in my covenant" (Heb 8:9). Before-state: covenant-breaking, hardened, under judgment. (2) Divine declaration of a new covenant — "the days are coming... I will make a new covenant" (Heb 8:8). The transition: God's initiative to address the failure. (3) Constitutional inscription — "I will put my laws into their minds and write them on their hearts" (Heb 8:10 — OBS-034-059). During: God acts within the inner person. (4) Relational identification — "I will be their God and they shall be my people" (Heb 8:10). After-state: covenantal belonging is established constitutionally. (5) Knowing — "they shall all know me, from the least to the greatest" (Jer 31:34). Final state: intimate knowing of God as the sustained product of the sequence. The sequence is: failure → divine initiative → inner inscription → belonging → knowing. This is the most fully articulated transformation sequence in the registry.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-005: T5 as a whole reveals that covenant is the most developmentally comprehensive of all characteristics in the programme's scope — it operates across all stages of formation (entry, formation, sanctifica…
findings.finding_value: T5 as a whole reveals that covenant is the most developmentally comprehensive of all characteristics in the programme's scope — it operates across all stages of formation (entry, formation, sanctification, eschatological fullness) and all scales of time (individual, generational, covenantal-historical, eschatological). The defining T5 finding is the two-mechanism contrast (Q&A-131): the Sinai covenant uses the external-demand mechanism (discipline and instruction); the new covenant uses the internal-inscription mechanism (Spirit-writing from within). This mechanism shift is not merely methodological — it represents a change in what the covenant does to the inner person. Under the old covenant, the person is required to bring their will to the covenant; under the new, the covenant brings a transformed will to the person. T5 confirms that covenant is not a static reality but a developing one — it moves through a sequence of inner states (Q&A-128: failure → initiative → inscription → belonging → knowing), and its eschatological trajectory points toward a fullness not yet realised but already grounded in the eternal covenant (Heb 13:20).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-020: T3 identifies the new covenant's faculty-level effect as the transformation of volition (from called-for to liberated — Q&A-085) and the production of covenantal knowing (Q&A-073). T5 identifies the d…
findings.finding_value: T3 identifies the new covenant's faculty-level effect as the transformation of volition (from called-for to liberated — Q&A-085) and the production of covenantal knowing (Q&A-073). T5 identifies the developmental sequence through which this transformation occurs (failure → inscription → belonging → knowing — Q&A-128) and the mechanism change (letter to Spirit — Q&A-131). The T3 × T5 synthesis: the faculty transformations identified in T3 (volition liberated, cognition/knowing produced) are the outcome of the developmental sequence and mechanism identified in T5. The sequence "inscription → belonging → knowing" (T5) describes how the specific faculty transformations of T3 are produced. The mechanism shift from letter to Spirit (T5) is the developmental mechanism that produces the volitional liberation (T3.6) and cognitive knowing (T3.2) that the new covenant delivers. T5 is the developmental story; T3 is the faculty-level outcome of that story.

findings.finding_value: T5 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has an eschatological orientation as its formative telos. The formation arc moves from constitutive endowment (Spirit and wisdom given to form inner-being capacity) through sustained covenantal narrative (the memory of received giving as formation environment) through suffering-testing (revealing whether inner-being giving is genuine) toward eschatological fullness ("oaks of righteousness," total communal transformation). The mechanisms are plural and context-specific — encounter (covenantal), gradual formation (endowing), sovereign reversal (eschatological) — revealing that formation is not a single pathway but a multi-modal process. The suffering relation is analytically significant: the characteristic is suffering-tested (revealed in human direction) and suffering-responsive (triggered in divine direction), showing that suffering is not incidental to the formation process but an integral context. T5.7 closes formally — no constitutional body deposit. What T5 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is constitutively developmental — its present forms anticipate and move toward a fullness that is not yet fully realised. Every giving is, in some sense, an eschatological act: it participates in the pattern of divine giving that is moving toward total, permanent, communal transformation.

Every sub-group evidences a sequence of inner states — the cluster's characteristics are not static qualities but developmental arcs. The most fully developed arc is M05-F's cascading comfort sequence (2Cor 1:3-7), which names five stages explicitly. The most complex arc is M05-G's formation sequence, which spans from divine calling through community formation to eschatological testing and inheritance.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — the Ezekiel stream (A2-002) describes a before/during/after sequence with exceptional clarity. Before: the person is righteous (the righteous person, tsad.diq). During: the turning point — the person "turns away from righteousness and does injustice" (Eze 18:24) — the volitional moment of departure. After: the former righteous deeds are not remembered; the person is assessed by their current state. The reversal sequence is equally clear: before: wicked. During: turning from wickedness. After: "he shall surely live" (Eze 18:21–22). The sequence is stark and explicit.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — before: under the weight of judgment (the condition that makes justification necessary); during: the act of faith that receives justification; after: the new standing of heir-status and freedom from condemnation (Tit 3:7). The before-during-after of justification maps directly onto the cluster's wider arc.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — before: the wrong has been done, the person bears the injustice. During: the period of the cry — persistent appeal to God for justice (Luk 18:3–8, VSG 944-001). After: God gives justice speedily (Luk 18:8) — the resolution. The sequence of D is: wrong endured → cry sustained → justice given.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — before: the person is either under external verdict or under self-verdict. During: the encounter with freedom — "has no one condemned you?" (Joh 8:10, VSG 4846-002). After: "neither do I condemn you; go, and from now on sin no more" (Joh 8:11) — the freed person is sent forward. The sequence: under verdict → encounter with the one who does not condemn → freed and commissioned.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — before: the person has received the declared reality of justification (through C). During: the act of reckoning — counting themselves dead to sin, alive to God (Rom 6:11). After: the consequent action — not letting sin reign (Rom 6:12). The sequence: declared reality → deliberate counting → changed behavioral orientation.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Yes — the hardening sequence in Rom 2:5 (VSG 3207-001): before: the opportunity to repent. During: the continued refusal — "hard and impenitent heart." After: the accumulated wrath. The sequence: refusal → hardening → accumulation of judgment.

**[CLUSTER — T5.2]** E. The cluster consistently provides before-during-after sequences across all sub-groups. The most explicit sequences are: the Ezekiel turning sequence (A2), the cry-and-response sequence (D), the encounter-and-freedom sequence (E), and the declared-reality-to-reckoned-action sequence (F). Together these sequences reveal that righteousness in M26 is not a static state — it is a dynamic reality that moves through the person in recognizable inner-state sequences.

findings.finding_value: Inner closure is maintained by sustained material prosperity without countervailing spiritual discipline. The sha.a.nan (at-ease) pattern is maintained by the ongoing absence of threat or challenge — the person who is never disturbed from their ease remains at ease. The wisdom tradition implies that the maintenance of inner closure requires no effort — it is the default outcome of unchallenged material prosperity.

findings.finding_value: The ordered character-wealth relationship is cultivated through the practices the wisdom tradition names: diligence in work (Pro 10:4), trust in the Lord (Pro 28:25 — ongoing orientation, not a single act), humility and fear of the Lord (Pro 22:4 — dispositions sustained over time), and the honouring of God with wealth (Pro 3:9 — ongoing practice of firstfruits). M46-C's ordered relationship requires active cultivation.

findings.finding_value: M01-A-VCG-04 (fear arising from witnessing God's deeds) shows a clear before-during-after sequence. Before: complacency or absence of fear (Exo 9:30: Pharaoh and servants do not yet fear the Lord). During: encounter with God's power (Exo 14:31: witnessing God's victory at the sea). After: fear and belief (Exo 14:31: "Israel feared the Lord and believed" — a settled new inner state following the encounter). Jon 1:5-16 shows the most complete sequence: before (mariners fearing the storm, crying to their own gods), during (encounter with Jonah's testimony and the storm's cessation), after (Jon 1:16: "the men feared the Lord greatly" and offered sacrifice and vows — a transformed reverential state).

M01-B-VCG-06 (commanded release of fear, anchor Isa 43:1) shows a before-during-after sequence structurally: before (fear gripping the inner person), during (divine word of identity and assurance spoken), after (the commanded release taking effect as trust replaces dread — implicit in the corpus as the intended outcome of each "do not fear" command). Dan 10:19 (M01-B-VCG-01: fear gripping Daniel → angel touching him and speaking → "inner person moves from fearful weakness to fortified courage") is the most explicit sequence.

M01-F-VCG-02 (anchor Job 3:25) shows the dread-sequence: before (dread sitting within as anticipated fear), during (the dreaded event materialising), after (the correspondence between fear and event — confirmation of the anticipatory dread). (2) *Decision point*: the will either resists (VCG-03: Joseph's refusal) or capitulates (1Sa 15:24: Saul yields). (4) *Post-act state B — consequences manifesting*: 1Ki 8:33/35 (defeat, drought). (1) *Prior state*: the person as a free moral subject with volitional capacity; (2) *The practice*: habitual sinning acts (Joh 8:34 — "everyone who practices sin"); (3) *The enslaved state*: "a slave to sin" — the constitutional consequence of the practice, governing the will. The sequence is: free moral subject → sustained practice of sinning → constitutional slave-condition. For the born-of-God liberation: (1) *Prior enslaved state*; (2) *New birth*: God's seed installs the counter-power; (3) *The cannot-keep-on-sinning state*: 1Jo 3:9 — the constitutional freedom from sustained sinning that the new birth produces.

**[CHAR-13]** E — Yes — multiple sequences. (1) *Record-accumulation sequence*: 1Sa 12:19 — "we have added to all our sins this evil" — the sequence is prior-record + new-sin → accumulated record; Isa 30:1 — "add sin to sin" — the deliberate accumulation sequence; Lev 26:18-28 — the covenant-discipline escalation sequence: sin → first-level discipline → continued sin → sevenfold → continued sin → fury-level. (2) *Recognition-to-remedy sequence*: Lev 4:23 — sin made known → person realises → brings offering; Num 5:6/7 — realises guilt → confesses → makes restitution. (3) *Erasure sequence*: Jer 31:34 — sin remembered → new covenant initiated → sin remembered no more; Eze 18:21 — wicked person → turns from all sins → keeps statutes → lives.

**[CHAR-14]** E — Yes — two parallel sequences. (1) *Levitical sequence*: sin committed → sin becomes known (Lev 4:14) → seeking initiated (offering brought) → priestly mediation enacted (atonement performed) → forgiveness granted (Lev 16:30 — clean before Lord) → restored relational standing. (2) *NT sequence*: sin accumulated → conviction (Spirit's work — Joh 16:8/9 in CHAR-11) → repentance (Act 2:38 — metanoeō) → baptism (Act 2:38 — outward) → forgiveness declared (Luk 7:48 — "your sins are forgiven") → Spirit received (Act 2:38) → love-orientation (Luk 7:47 — "she loved much") → life replacing death (Col 2:13).

**[CHAR-15]** E — Yes — a trajectory across the corpus. (1) *Active sinning phase*: Psa 78:17 — "sinned still more... rebelling" — persistent sinning despite divine provision; (2) *Prolonged condition*: Isa 64:5 — "in our sins we have been a long time" — the sinning has become the settled state; (3) *Consequence and doom*: Jer 8:14 — "doomed to perish... poisoned water" — the accumulated sinning produces catastrophic external consequences; (4) *Corporate recognition and confession*: 1Ki 8:47 — "turn their heart... repent and plead... 'We have sinned'" — the consequence drives the recognition; (5) *Divine restoration promise*: Eze 37:23 — cleansed, restored covenant-people identity.

**[CHAR-16]** E — Yes — two opposing sequences. (1) *Formation-to-extremity sequence*: individual sinning acts → social recognition as sinner → habitual pattern → extreme-type moral character (Gen 13:13 — Sodom; Amo 9:8/10 — sinful kingdom); (2) *Recognition-to-restoration sequence*: proximity to holiness → conscience recognition (Luk 5:8 — "I am a sinful man") → self-abasement and plea (Luk 18:13 — "be merciful to me, a sinner") → repentance (Luk 15:7 — "one sinner who repents") → return (Psa 51:13 — "sinners will return to you") → cosmic joy (Luk 15:10).

**[CHAR-17]** E — Yes — the most explicit inner-state sequence in M10 is in Lev 5:2-5: (1) violation committed (outer act); (2) "hidden from him" (inner unawareness — no guilt-state yet); (3) "when he comes to know it" (knowledge event — guilt-trigger); (4) "realizes his guilt" (guilt-recognition — guilt-state active); (5) "confesses the sin he has committed" (speech-act — guilt expressed outward); followed by the prescribed offering (outer remedy). A second sequence: Hos 5:15's broader arc: Israel in sin → God withdraws → distress → "acknowledge their guilt" → "seek my face" → God returns.

**[CHAR-18]** E — Yes — two opposing sequences. (1) *Accumulation-to-ruin sequence*: heart takes in idols (Eze 14:3 — VCG-08 origin) → outer sinning acts (VCG-04 — personal crime) → divine record maintained (VCG-03 — Hos 13:12 — "bound up") → weight accumulates (VCG-05 — Psa 38:4 — "gone over my head") → self-destructive force (VCG-07 — Pro 5:22 — "held fast in cords") → ruin (Eze 18:30 — "lest iniquity be your ruin"); (2) *Confession-to-removal sequence*: iniquity acknowledged (Lev 26:40) → heart humbled (Lev 26:41) → priestly bearing (VCG-01 — Lev 16:21) → divine forgiveness (VCG-06 — Isa 40:2; Jer 31:34) → blessed state (Psa 32:2 — "no iniquity counted against him").

**[CHAR-19]** E — Yes — two opposing sequences. (1) *Transgression-to-enslavement sequence*: known boundary (Rom 4:15 — law required) → will crosses (Isa 1:2 — "they have rebelled") → transgression speaks from heart (Psa 36:1) → accumulation toward threshold (Amos 1:3 — counted) → enslaving grip (Pro 29:6 — ensnared; Psa 19:13 — dominion threatened) → yoke-burden (Lam 1:14) → systemic inner collapse (Isa 1:5 — head sick, heart faint); (2) *Recognition-to-restoration sequence*: self-knowing (Psa 51:3 — "I know my transgressions") → confession (Psa 32:5; Pro 28:13) → volitional turning (Eze 18:28) → divine blotting-out (Isa 43:25) → blessedness (Psa 32:1) → teaching capacity (Psa 51:13).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The corpus evidences a clear three-stage sequence. (1) *Pre-awareness state*: the person acts without knowledge of the moral reality of the act — the will is engaged but uninformed; no inner-being response to sinning is possible because the sin is not yet known to the person. (2) *Disclosure event*: the sin "becomes known" (Lev 4:14 — adjacent; Lev 5:5 — "when he realizes his guilt"; Num 22:34 — the angel discloses) — the morally relevant fact arrives, triggering conscience. (3) *Post-realisation state*: conscience engaged, guilt recognised, confession made (Lev 5:5), remedy sought (Num 15:27), will oriented toward reversal (Num 22:34). The transition from stage 1 to stage 2 is the defining inner-being event of the characteristic — the knowledge-arrival that transforms inadvertent sinning into a consciously addressed moral reality.

**[CHAR-20]** E — Yes — two sequences. (1) *Faithlessness-to-judgment sequence*: spirit-level unguarded (Mal 2:15 inverse) → will's allegiance-transfer (1Ch 5:25 — whoring after gods) → covenant-breaking act (Lev 26:40 — "treachery they committed") → divine face-hiding (Eze 39:23) → exile and shame (Dan 9:7; 1Ch 9:1); (2) *Recognition-to-restoration sequence*: community appalled (Ezr 9:4) → corporate mourning (Ezr 10:6 — Ezra fasting) → confession (Ezr 10:2/10 — "we have broken faith") → humble acknowledgment (Lev 26:40 — naming generational treachery) → covenant-remembered (Lev 26:42) → secure dwelling and forgotten shame (Eze 39:26).

**[CHAR-21]** E — Yes — two sequences. (1) *Perversion-to-destruction sequence*: perverted heart (Pro 6:14 — inner origin) → devises evil → sows discord (outer expression) → overthrown (Pro 21:12 — judgment); or: deceitful desire (Eph 4:22 — desire-level) → corrupt old self → enslaved to corruption (2Pe 2:19) → destroyed by instinct (Jude 10); (2) *Recognition-to-renewal sequence*: confession of perversity (1Ki 8:47; Dan 9:5) → movement toward God (1Ki 8:48 — "return to you with all their mind and with all their heart") → putting off old self (Eph 4:22) → renewal of mind's spirit (Eph 4:23) → participation in divine nature (2Pe 1:4).

**[CHAR-22]** E — Yes — two sequences. (1) *Injustice-to-judgment sequence*: God-ignorance (Job 18:21 — "knows not God") → heart-devising of wrong (Psa 58:2; Psa 64:6) → enacting with hands (Psa 58:2 — "hands deal out violence") → sowing injustice (Pro 22:8) → reaping calamity (Pro 22:8) → God remembering (Rev 18:5) → judgment (2Pe 2:9); (2) *Cessation-to-life sequence*: acknowledging unseen iniquity (Job 34:32 — "teach me what I do not see") → committing to cease (Job 34:32 — "I will do it no more") → restoring pledges (Eze 33:15) → not doing injustice (Eze 18:8) → walking in statutes of life (Eze 33:15) → living (Eze 33:15 — "he shall surely live").

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. The corpus evidences a clear sequence across the paradigm cases. (1) *Pre-confession state*: sin committed, conscience not yet or just beginning to engage. 2Sa 24:10 — David has numbered the people; the heart-striking occurs afterward. Luk 15:17 (context) — the prodigal "came to himself" — the moment of conscience-engagement that precedes the inner resolution. (2) *The confessional moment*: the conscience-to-speech movement — heart struck → "David said to the Lord: I have sinned greatly" (2Sa 24:10); "I will arise and go to my father" → "Father, I have sinned" (Luk 15:18/21). (3) *Post-confession state*: plea for mercy (2Sa 24:10 — "please take away the iniquity"), expectation of divine action (Mic 7:9 — "until he pleads my cause"), or relational restoration (Luk 15:22–24 — the father's reception).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The corpus evidences a developmental sequence across the different modes. (1) *Initial state*: the person sins and the conscience does not register it accurately — either through ignorance of God (1Cor 15:34), through the fear of God absent (Ecc 8:12), or through active self-interested denial (Jer 2:35). (2) *Developmental state*: repeated sinning without conscience-registration habituates the inner person to conscience-absent operation — "does evil a hundred times" (Ecc 8:12) — the pattern deepens. (3) *Advanced state*: the conscience suppression has become a constitutional feature — "warped and sinful" (Tit 3:11); the person is "self-condemned" without knowing it. (4) *Judgment announced but not received*: the external prophetic word declares judgment (Jer 2:35; 16:10), but the conscience-suppressed person still does not register it — the external input fails to break through the suppression.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes — the corpus traces a developmental sequence across the Kings pattern. (1) *Initial state*: the sinful course inherited and not rejected — "as his fathers had done" (2Ki 15:9) — the will's passive acceptance. (2) *Developmental state*: "did not depart from" — the will's persistent non-departure becomes the settled pattern across a reign. (3) *Advanced state*: "clung to" (2Ki 3:3 — *davaq*) — the will actively attaches to the sinful course; the attachment is no longer merely passive. (4) *Constitutional state*: "stubborn shoulder and stiffened their neck" (Neh 9:29) — the refusal has become a bodily-metaphor constitutional posture. (5) *Terminal state*: Heb 10:26 — deliberate sinning after full knowledge, with the sacrifice foreclosed — the refusal has reached the point where the reversal mechanism is described as unavailable.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes — the corpus evidences a developmental sequence, most clearly in Exo 9:34 and the Hosea passages. (1) *Initial sinning*: the first act that begins the pattern — Exo 9:34 — "sinned yet again" implies prior sinning; Hos 10:9 — "from the days of Gibeah" — a named historical starting point. (2) *Hardening/entrenchment*: Exo 9:34 — "hardened his heart" — the sinning produces hardening; the will is reshaped by the act of sinning. (3) *Institutionalisation*: Hos 8:11 — altars for sinning becoming altars that produce more sinning — the inner orientation externalises into structures. (4) *Generational persistence*: Hos 10:9 — "there they have continued" — the pattern sustains across generations. (5) *Epistemic blindness*: 1Jo 3:6 — "never seen or known him" — the advanced condition of habitual defection in which the person cannot perceive God.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The corpus evidences a clear developmental sequence. (1) *Leader's personal sinning established*: the leader first sins personally ("walked in the way of Jeroboam" — 1Ki 16:26); (2) *Authority-based transmission*: the leader uses their authority position to transmit the sinning direction ("made Israel to sin" — Hiphil causative across the Kings corpus); (3) *Community's orientation redirected*: "drove Israel from following the Lord" (2Ki 17:21) — the community's inner orientation is reshaped; (4) *Structural embedding*: sinning institutions built (high places, altars — 2Ki 23:15; Jer 32:35); (5) *Generational persistence*: the transmitted direction is sustained and sometimes escalated across generations (1Ki 22:52; 1Ki 14:22 — "more than all that their fathers had done"); (6) *Divine abandonment as consequence*: "he will give Israel up" (1Ki 14:16).

**[CHAR-8]** E — A limited sequence is evidenced, most clearly in 2Ch 21:10's causal structure. (1) *Prior state*: the governing relationship intact — the nations are under governing authority (implied by the revolt's occurrence). (2) *Inner causative event*: 2Ch 21:10 — the ruler forsakes the Lord; the inner spiritual abandonment precedes and enables the political fragmentation. (3) *The revolt event*: the decisive act of pa.sha — Moab rebelling (2Ki 1:1), Edom revolting (2Ki 8:20). (4) *Permanent post-revolt state*: "to this day" — the broken political relationship as the persistent reality. The sequence is: intact-authority-relationship → inner spiritual abandonment (governing authority) → political revolt → permanent fracture.

**[CHAR-9]** E — Yes — most clearly from VCG-01 and 1Ti 1:13. (1) *Inner corruption state*: the heart's moral corruption as the pre-speech state — Mat 15:19 — "out of the heart come evil thoughts" — the prior inner state before the speech act. (2) *The affective enablers*: Eph 4:31 — bitterness, wrath, anger as the emotional pre-speech state. (3) *The speech act*: the externalisation through the mouth — "slander" as the named output. (4) *The post-speech consequence*: relational damage (VCG-01), judicial condemnation (VCG-02 — Mar 14:64), or permanent foreclosure (Mat 12:31). Additionally, 1Ti 1:13 evidences a reversal sequence: blasphemer (prior state) → mercy received → faith and love (post-mercy state, implied by the apostolic context).

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The evidence from multiple VCGs maps a discernible sequence of inner states. Drawing on VCG-07 (directional orientation) and VCG-06 (instability and self-destruction), the sequence is: (1) Initial volitional entry — "do not enter the path of the wicked" (Pro 4:14) — the first stage is a choice; (2) Settled orientation — the person "walks in counsel of the wicked, stands in the way of sinners, sits in the seat of scoffers" (Psa 1:1 — a progressively deepening alignment); (3) Active God-exclusion — practical atheism consolidates (Psa 10:4; 10:13 — "all his thoughts are 'There is no God'"); (4) Inner instability and self-bondage — the characteristic generates its own cords (Pro 5:22), produces chronic dread (Pro 10:24), and inner torment (Job 15:20); (5) Final dissolution — "the wicked will be no more" (Psa 37:10), name rots (Pro 10:7), reduced to ashes (Mal 4:3). This sequence is not perfectly ordered in every verse but the pattern is discernible across the 190V corpus.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The evidence maps discernible sequential patterns. The deterioration sequence: (1) constitutional evil baseline (Mat 7:11 — VCG-02 — "you who are evil"); (2) settled inner malice and vice-saturation (Rom 1:29 — VCG-05 — "filled with all manner"); (3) defiled conscience making approach to God impossible (Heb 10:22 — VCG-06); (4) progressive deterioration (2Ti 3:13 — VCG-06 — "from bad to worse"). The remedial sequence: (1) exposure and conviction (Act 8:22 — VCG-05 — "repent of this wickedness"); (2) active stripping away (Jam 1:21 — VCG-05 — "put away all filthiness and rampant wickedness"); (3) receptive receiving (Jam 1:21 — VCG-05 — "receive with meekness the implanted word"); (4) cleansed constitutional state (Heb 10:22 — VCG-06 — "hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience"); (5) genuine approach to God restored.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. VCG-04 (11 verses) is specifically the conscience-sequence evidence, documenting the characteristic's inner-state progression. The deepening sequence: (1) inner moral knowledge present but conscience beginning to be suppressed — Deu 27:15 (vc=65937 — VCG-04): the person sets up the idol in secret while knowing it is wrong; (2) abomination committed with partial conscience-engagement; (3) full conscience-silencing — Jer 6:15 (vc=1680 — VCG-04); Jer 8:12 (vc=1696 — VCG-04): "not at all ashamed; they did not know how to blush"; (4) accumulated weight — Eze 44:13 (vc=66003 — VCG-04): abominations as permanent burden; (5) eschatological exclusion — Rev 21:27 (vc=22 — VCG-05). The restoration sequence (Ezekiel): (1) divine action restores memory — Eze 36:31 (vc=1681); (2) self-loathing emerges; (3) repentance-command — Eze 14:6 (vc=65984); (4) turning from abominations.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. The Ezekiel VCG-05 corpus (43V) documents the sequence with particular intensity. The deepening sequence: (1) initial volitional attraction and choice — Isa 66:3 (vc=1633 — VCG-04): "they have chosen their own ways"; (2) heart and soul attachment forming — Eze 11:21 (vc=1631 — VCG-05): heart going after detestable things; (3) eye-feasting habit entrenching — Eze 20:7-8 (vc=1634; 65911 — VCG-05): eyes feasting, unwilling to cast away; (4) moral gravity lost — Eze 8:17 (vc=65980 — VCG-05): treating abomination as trivial; (5) progressive deepening — Eze 8:13; 8:15 (VCG-05): still greater abominations; (6) constitutional transformation — Hos 9:10 (vc=1632 — VCG-04): becoming detestable; (7) memory lost — Eze 16:22 (vc=65985 — VCG-05): not remembering origins; (8) divine withdrawal — Eze 5:11 (vc=65969 — VCG-05); (9) judgment — Eze 5:9 (vc=65968 — VCG-05).

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. The evidence documents a deepening sequence across the VCGs. (1) Initial volitional entry: Job 36:21 (vc=38216 — VCG-04): "this you have chosen rather than affliction" — the will chooses iniquity over the harder righteous path. (2) Active nocturnal devising: Psa 36:4 (vc=38235 — VCG-02): "plots trouble while on his bed" — the cognitive scheming mode is established. (3) Heart accumulating iniquity: Psa 41:6 (vc=38236 — VCG-04): "his heart gathers iniquity" — the condition of accumulation. (4) Wisdom displaced: Psa 36:3 (vc=38234 — VCG-04): "ceased to act wisely and do good." (5) Conscience deadened: Pro 30:20 (vc=38222 — VCG-04): "I have done no wrong." (6) Iniquity seeking dominion: Psa 119:133 (vc=38227 — VCG-04): the will increasingly under iniquity's control. (7) Terminal collapse: Psa 36:12 (vc=38233 — VCG-04): "fallen… unable to rise."

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes. VCG-01 documents the sequence with unusual explicitness. The Rev 16 sequence (vc=14352; 14350; 14353 — VCG-01): (1) First judgment (scorching heat) → cursing God's name + refusal to repent or give glory (Rev 16:9); (2) Second judgment (darkness, pain, sores) → cursing the God of heaven + refusal to repent of deeds (Rev 16:11); (3) Third judgment (catastrophic hail) → cursing God for the plague because it was so severe (Rev 16:21). The sequence shows: escalating judgment → escalating defiance, with each stage showing the will more fixed in its anti-God orientation. Jude 8 (vc=14354 — VCG-01): the prior state that enables blasphemy: sensory self-indulgence → authority-rejection → blasphemy — a three-stage inner sequence from indulgence through rejection to verbal defiance.

**[CLUSTER]** E — All six characteristics document sequences of inner states, confirming the cluster's process-character. The sequences share structural similarity across the six: initial inner-condition (characteristic established) → progressive deepening through sustained operation → terminal consequences. The most detailed sequences are in Chars 4 and 6. Char 4: initial volitional attraction → heart/soul attachment → eye-feasting habit → moral gravity lost → progressive deepening → constitutional transformation → memory suppressed → divine withdrawal → judgment (Eze 8:9-17 escalating vision). Char 6: initial posture (self-indulgence + authority-rejection — Jude 8) → blasphemy established → judgment falling → blasphemous response deepening across three plague-events (Rev 16:9 → 16:11 → 16:21). The cluster's shared sequence structure: prior enabling conditions → initial characteristic formation → deepening through sustained operation → the characteristic's own expression reinforcing the inner condition (feedback) → terminal state.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The sequence is evidenced most completely in the corpse-contact sub-register (M10c-A-VCG-07) and the skin-disease sub-register (M10c-B-VCG-02/03). For corpse-contact: before — clean, eligible for worship participation; during — unclean, barred from community access, the condition "still on him" (Num 19:13), grief at exclusion (Num 9:7); after — clean, access restored through the prescribed sprinkling and washing (Num 19:19). The sequence is: clean → defilement-event → condition imposed → conscience-awareness (Lev 5:2-3) → will-engagement (pursue remedy or refuse) → remedy applied (washing, waiting, sprinkling) → condition resolved → clean restored. For the disease register: the sequence includes a longer "during" of examination, verdict, isolation, and waiting (Lev 13-14, M10c-B-VCG-02/03).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes. The sequence most fully documented in the corpus runs through VCG-02: (1) Heart-level desire generated internally (Rom 1:24 — "lusts of their hearts"); (2) divine judicial withdrawal as response to prior rejection (Rom 1:24 — "God gave them up"); (3) the condition of impurity entered as the result (Rom 1:24 — "to impurity"); (4) bodily dishonour as the external expression (Rom 1:24 — "dishonoring of their bodies"); (5) escalation — lawlessness generates more lawlessness (Rom 6:19 — "leading to more lawlessness"); (6) conscience silenced — callousness (Eph 4:19 — "become callous"); (7) active moral appetite substituting for suppressed conscience (Eph 4:19 — "greedy to practice every kind of impurity"). The positive-inverse sequence (VCG-05) runs: not defiling oneself (Rev 14:4) → following the Lamb → being redeemed as firstfruits → eschatological fullness.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. The prophetic corpus (especially Ezekiel) documents a clear sequence. (1) Corporate covenantal fidelity as the baseline (Eze 18:6 — the righteous man who does not defile). (2) Inner desire-driven departure toward idols (Eze 20:7/18/30/31 — the repeated commands against defiling with Egypt's/fathers' idols, showing a persistent pull). (3) Corporate acts of defiling — idols installed in sanctuary (Jer 7:30), whoredom with nations (Eze 23:7), sexual violations within community (Eze 22:11). (4) Corporate defilement-state established — land contaminated (Eze 36:17/18), sanctuary desecrated (Eze 5:11), name defiled (Eze 43:8), divine presence withdrawn (Eze 5:11). (5) Judgment and exile — community expelled (Lam 4:15), named "a filthy thing" (Lam 1:17), eating unclean food in Assyria (Hos 9:3). (6) Eschatological restoration — memory triggers self-loathing (Eze 20:43), divine cleansing promised (Eze 37:23, Zec 13:1), holy city restored (Isa 52:1).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes. Three stages across VCGs -01, -02, -03. (1) Pre-possession: the person in their proper self-possessed state (implied by what the spirit disrupts — communal life severed in Mar 5:2 implies prior communal belonging; family relationship disrupted in Luk 9:42 implies prior intact family bond). (2) Possessed/defiled: the condition of domination, faculty-suppression, communal severance, and bodily subjugation — Mar 1:23, Mar 5:2, Mar 7:25, Mar 9:25, Luk 4:33, Luk 8:29, Luk 9:42. (3) Restored/whole: the healed state after expulsion — Luk 6:18 ("cured"), Luk 9:42 ("healed... gave him back to his father"), Act 5:16 ("all healed").

**[CLUSTER]** E — All four characteristics evidence a sequence of inner states (before, during, after), but the number of stages and the character of the "during" state differ. Characteristic 1 is the simplest: three stages (clean → defiled → restored-clean), with the will's position at the transition between defiled and restored as the morally critical point. Characteristic 2 is the most complex: seven documented stages in the descending sequence (desire → judicial release → condition → bodily dishonour → escalating lawlessness → callousness → active appetite) plus the ascending positive-inverse (not defiling → following the Lamb → eschatological firstfruits). Characteristic 3 has six stages: covenantal fidelity → desire-directed departure → corporate defiling acts → defilement-state established → exile and expulsion → memory-generated self-loathing and divine cleansing. Characteristic 4 is the simplest positive sequence: wholeness → spirit-dominated defilement → restored wholeness. The cluster's sequence complexity gradient: Characteristic 1 (3 stages, will as turning point) → Characteristic 3 (6 stages, corporate-eschatological arc) → Characteristic 2 (7 descending stages + positive sequence, most self-reinforcing) → Characteristic 4 (3 stages, simplest but most radically transformative). The complexity of the sequence correlates with the volitional engagement: the more the characteristic engages the person's own will (Chars 2, 3), the more stages the sequence has, because the will generates its own momentum and the sequence deepens before resolving.

questions.question_text: What are those states, and what does the sequence reveal about how this characteristic works?

findings.session_b_note:
Drawing from both sequences:

**States named or strongly implied:**
1. Sin-state (the transgression that creates the debt)
2. Guilt-state (the legitimate moral claim registered — conscience, inner knowing of wrong)
3. Seeking/intercession state (the inner posture of appeal toward God)
4. Forgiven-state (afesis — the condition of release, the claim cancelled)
5. Love-orientation (the relational disposition produced in the recipient)
6. Reverence/fear (the awe produced by encountering the depth of God's forgiveness-capacity)
7. Hope-orientation (the sustained forward-looking posture grounded in known forgiveness)
8. Horizontal-giving capacity (the enabled ability to extend forgiveness to others)

**What the sequence reveals:** Forgiveness does not operate as a single moment but as a **movement through an ordered series of inner states**. The sequence reveals:
- The before-states (guilt, grievance) are real and named — forgiveness does not pretend they are not there
- The access-states require genuine inner engagement — the person must orient toward reception
- The after-states are multiple and developmental — the immediate response (love, fear, blessedness) differs from the sustained effect (hope, horizontal-capacity)
- The sequence is **generative not merely corrective** — it does not only remove the guilt-state but produces new positive inner states not present before

findings.session_b_note:
The sequences together reveal a common pattern: encounter with grace → creaturely recognition response (fear, mourning, prostration) → inner transformation (tenderheartedness, standing, capacity) → outward expression (forgiving, gracious speech, ministry). The creaturely recognition response is consistently present as the transitional state — the inner moment of registering the weight of what is given — before transformation settles. Grace does not bypass the person's recognition; it requires and produces it as part of the sequence.

*New finding: the creaturely recognition response as a consistent transitional state in all grace-sequences is not previously named as a T5 observation. A significant structural finding.*

The sequences together reveal a common pattern: encounter with grace → creaturely recognition response (fear, mourning, prostration) → inner transformation (tenderheartedness, standing, capacity) → outward expression (forgiving, gracious speech, ministry). The creaturely recognition response is consistently present as the transitional state — the inner moment of registering the weight of what is given — before transformation settles. Grace does not bypass the person's recognition; it requires and produces it as part of the sequence.

*New finding: the creaturely recognition response as a consistent transitional state in all grace-sequences is not previously named as a T5 observation. A significant structural finding.*

findings.session_b_note:
The sequence reveals three things about how compassion works:

**Compassion is bottom-up and inside-out.** The sequence in the giver begins in the body (gut-stirring, heart-recoiling) before it engages the soul (character disposition) and the will (choice of action). This confirms the constitutional movement sequence assembled at T2.10: compassion does not begin with a cognitive or volitional determination. It begins with a body-event triggered by perception and moves upward and outward.

**The before-state is constitutive of the quality of the during-state.** The eusplanchnos (tender heart) pre-condition is not merely a nice-to-have antecedent — it is what allows the somatic stirring to arise naturally and fully. A person without the pre-condition of inner tenderness may still choose to act compassionately (volitionally), but the full splanchnizō movement — the involuntary body-prior arousal — requires the inner constitution to be already oriented toward the other. The quality of the compassion-during depends on the formation of the before-state.

**The after-state feeds back into the before-state of future compassion.** The experience of giving compassion — being moved, acting, extending — reinforces and deepens the character qualities (eusplanchnos, ra.chum) that constitute the before-state for future encounters. This creates a formative cycle: compassion-experience deepens the inner constitution that enables richer compassion-experience in the future. The character of the compassionate person is not static — it is progressively formed through the experience of being moved and moving toward others.

findings.session_b_note:
The five states are named above. The sequence reveals two structurally significant things:

1. **The threshold function of contrition**: The contrite state (stage 2) is not the end of the sequence but the threshold — it is the inner-being condition from which the longing (stage 3) arises and toward which the divine response (stage 4) moves. Contrition is neither the first movement (that is the crushing) nor the final state (that is restoration). It is the threshold through which the sequence passes.

2. **Contrition as the gate of receptivity**: The sequence reveals that without the contrite posture (stage 2), the divine response (stage 4) does not move toward the person — the hardened alternative (Jer 44:10) shows a person who skips stage 2 and therefore never reaches stage 4. The contrite posture is the constitutive gate through which divine reviving reaches the inner being.

*New finding: contrition's position in the sequence — as threshold and gate of receptivity rather than as beginning or end — clarifies its functional role in the transformation process. This assembly from the sequence data has not been made in prior analysis.*

findings.session_b_note:
The sequences reveal a common structural logic: **fellowship operates as a prerequisite-to-participation mechanism** (finding 062-SEQUE-001). In every sequence:

1. Something must be received, escaped, or entered first (promise, encounter with Christ, proclamation, wound).
2. The fellowship itself is then entered or experienced.
3. The fellowship produces a transformed state (divine nature participation, resurrection orientation, new fellowship bond, cleansed inner condition).

The sequence is always: enabling condition → fellowship entry → transformed outcome. Fellowship is not a state the person is already in; it is entered through a prior enabling condition and produces a further transformed state beyond itself. This is structurally important: fellowship is a *movement* rather than a *position*.

findings.session_b_note: The two sequences reveal that goodness works through different mechanisms depending on its register. The positive arc (encounter → trust → reorientation → overflow) reveals that goodness works by producing a progressive deepening of inner orientation — encounter leads to trust, trust leads to stable orientation, orientation leads to outward expression. The characteristic builds from first contact to sustained character. The moral awareness arc (memory → recognition → loathing → repentance) reveals that goodness works through the confrontation with its own absence — the standard of the good, when encountered, produces awareness of not-goodness that is itself a mechanism of transformation. Goodness therefore works both through positive encounter (receiving divine goodness) and through negative recognition (confronting one's absence of goodness). The sequence also reveals the role of time: both arcs are extended through time, not instantaneous — goodness is a formative characteristic, not a momentary experience. (OBS-067-OBS-025, OBS-067-OBS-029, OBS-067-OBS-035)

findings.session_b_note: The three sequences (Q&A-202) reveal a common underlying structure: love is not the starting point of the inner-being movement but the outcome of a prior transaction. In the forgiveness sequence: guilt is resolved by forgiveness, and love flows from the resolution. In the divine-love sequence: lovelessness is met by divine love, and responsive love emerges. In the receiving-rest sequence: striving is displaced by received love, and rest follows. The common revelation: love is the product of reception rather than the self-generated initiating state. The person does not begin with love and then encounter God; they encounter God's love and then love in return. This sequence has a directional implication for formation: love cannot be trained from the outside in (as if instruction alone could produce it); it must be received first, and then expressed. The before-state is always some form of lacking — guilt, lovelessness, or striving — that love's prior reception resolves.
