**[CHAR-3]** E — The negative: CHAR-3's active form represents a corruption of the worth-recognition capacity that formation is meant to heal. The positive: learning to see and honour the worth of others — especially the poor, the weak, those the world despises — is part of the formation of the image-bearer toward the likeness of God. Jam 2:6's condemnation of dishonoring the poor is precisely a formation instruction: the community must learn to see worth where the world sees none.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — CHAR-4 in its functioning form is a formation-essential faculty: the person who cannot recognise what is shameful cannot be formed toward moral maturity. Paul's renunciation of shameful ways (2Cor 4:2) as the basis for credible ministry shows CHAR-4 as a prerequisite for authentic Christian formation and community life. The revival of CHAR-4 is itself a formation goal: the corrective-shame passages in CHAR-1's M07-C material (1Cor 6:5; 15:34) are attempts to reactivate the community's dormant CHAR-4 capacity.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — CHAR-5 participates in sanctification through the formation it requires: the person who receives contempt and responds with blessing rather than retaliation (1Pe 3:9) is being formed in the direction of Christ's own response to contempt. The protective-absence cases (Rut 2:15; 1Sa 25:7/15) show CHAR-5's prevention as an act of character formation in the protector — restraining oneself from contemptuous treatment of the vulnerable is a formative moral practice.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — CHAR-6 participates in the longer arc of character formation: the sustained maintenance of innocence (Psa 73:13 — "I have kept my heart clean") over time through suffering and apparent futility is itself a formative practice. The person who maintains moral integrity even when it seems unrewarded is being formed in the direction of genuine covenant faithfulness — the formation that produces the character capable of the sanctuary encounter where innocence is vindicated.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — M07 is a formation-essential cluster: its characteristics are the primary moral-spiritual dynamics that formation must engage. Formation through M07 operates along three axes at the cluster level. (1) Reception of corrective shame — learning to receive shame's corrective signal (Char 1 M07-C/B), recognise and renounce the shameful (Char 4), and maintain the moral integrity that protects against guilt-shame (Char 6). These three axes constitute the formation process's conscience-dimension. (2) Protection from unjust shame — grounded enough in God's worth-assignment to receive unjust shame, contempt, and dishonour without being defined by them (Chars 1 M07-A, 3, 5). (3) Learning to see worth — developing the worth-recognition capacity that Chars 3 and 5 presuppose: seeing the worth of the poor, the despised, and the vulnerable as God sees it (Jam 2:6; 1Cor 1:28). Formation is incomplete without engaging all three axes.

questions.question_text: In this verse, is the characteristic oriented toward an eschatological fullness — a future state toward which its present operation points — and what does its present experience anticipate of that fullness? Record none if no such orientation is shown.

findings.session_b_note:
The data provides partial evidence for an eschatological dimension:

**Jer 31:34 as eschatological anticipation:** The new covenant declaration — "I will forgive their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more" — carries an eschatological quality. OBS-064-017 names it as "the most unconditional register of divine forgiveness in the OT." The permanence of the forgiveness ("rendered non-recallable") and the directness of the God-knowing ("they shall all know me") point toward a fullness that transcends the current order. This verse is already partially eschatological in its register — it names a future state of complete covenantal restoration.

**Psa 130:5-7 as eschatological hope:** The Psalm moves from present forgiveness (Psa 130:4) to future hope ("I wait for the Lord... with him is plentiful redemption, and he will redeem Israel from all his iniquities" — Psa 130:8). The present experience of forgiveness is explicitly oriented toward a future fullness of redemption. Q040 answer draws this: "forgiveness as the ground of hope."

**The outer limit as eschatological boundary:** Mar 3:29 — "guilty of an eternal sin." The term "eternal" (aiōnios) places the unforgivable sin in eschatological register — the permanent guilt-state extends beyond the present order. By contrast, received forgiveness implies an eschatological release — the guilt-state does not persist into eternity for the forgiven person.

*Gap noted:* The data does not explicitly examine what the completed experience of forgiveness looks like in eschatological fullness — whether the present forgiven-state is a partial foretaste or complete. This is a live gap requiring Session D attention.

findings.session_b_note:
The data provides partial eschatological evidence, strongest in the sumpaschō/syndoxazō frame and in the polusplanchnos/telos language of Jas 5:11.

**Rom 8:17 (sumpaschō → syndoxazō):** SD-012 identifies this as the clearest eschatological trajectory in the data. Present fellow-suffering (sumpaschō — a compassion-solidarity act) is oriented toward future shared glorification (syndoxazō). The compassion-solidarity of the present age is moving toward an eschatological fullness in which that solidarity is transformed into shared glory. Compassion as suffering-with is therefore not merely a present-age virtue — it is participation in a trajectory that ends in glorification.

**Jas 5:11 (polusplanchnos + telos):** The verse explicitly names the "purpose (telos) of the Lord" in the context of God's deep compassion and human endurance. The telos is referenced but not described — it is the intended end toward which the arc of suffering and divine compassion is oriented. The eschatological signal is present but not developed in the data.

**The everlasting chesed:** Lam 3:22-23 — "his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning." The perpetual renewal of divine chesed carries an implicit eschatological trajectory: if chesed never ceases and is perpetually renewed, it is oriented toward a fullness that has not yet arrived. The present experience of divine compassion is a foretaste of an inexhaustible reality.

**What is missing (P):** The data does not contain a verse that explicitly names compassion itself as moving toward an eschatological fullness in the human person — as a characteristic that the person will possess or experience more completely in the age to come. The eschatological orientation is present but underdeveloped for the human person specifically. SD-012 partially addresses this; the question of compassion's eschatological fullness in the human remains an open gap.

findings.session_b_note:
The evidence carries a forward orientation, as noted at T0.2 Prompt 3 (new finding established there). The eschatological indicators:

**Phili 3:10-11:** The fellowship of Christ's sufferings is explicitly oriented toward *the resurrection of the dead* (v.11, adjacent context). The fellowship trajectory is: suffering → death → resurrection. The resurrection is the eschatological terminus of the fellowship-with-Christ sequence.

**2Pe 1:4:** Divine nature participation enables escape from corruption and progressive participation in divine nature — a trajectory that points toward the full removal of corruption and the completion of divine likeness. The present experience is participatory entry into what will be possessed in fullness eschatologically.

**Ecc 9:4 — present fellowship grounding hope:** *He who is joined with all the living has hope* — hope is named as the affective orientation of present fellowship. Hope is by definition forward-facing.

**Gap:** No verse in the registry explicitly addresses a future fullness of fellowship beyond resurrection (new creation, eternal fellowship). The eschatological data is present but partial — it extends to resurrection but not beyond.

findings.session_b_note: Partial eschatological evidence is present. Eph 2:7 ("so that in the coming ages he might show the immeasurable riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus") explicitly places chrēstotēs in a future-oriented eschatological frame — God's chrēstotēs will be displayed in its fullness in the coming ages. This names an eschatological trajectory: present experience of divine kindness anticipates its future unrestricted display. 2Th 1:11 ("fulfil every resolve for good") implies a completion — God's completing act brings present goodness-resolve to its fullness. However, the specifically eschatological texture of goodness (what it will be in the new creation, what fullness means) is not directly described in the anchor verses beyond these two instances. The trajectory is indicated but not fully developed. (OBS-067-OBS-008, OBS-067-OBS-016, SBF-067-Q006)

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-005: T5 as a whole reveals that goodness is one of the most developmentally rich characteristics in the programme. Three transformation types (condition change, orientation change, character transformation…
findings.finding_value: T5 as a whole reveals that goodness is one of the most developmentally rich characteristics in the programme. Three transformation types (condition change, orientation change, character transformation — Q&A-123), two distinct transformation sequences (positive encounter arc and moral awareness arc — Q&A-126), and three context-differentiated transformation mechanisms (encounter, Spirit-infusion, recognition-confrontation — Q&A-129) together produce a portrait of a characteristic that reaches the person through multiple developmental pathways depending on their condition and context. The formation/sanctification section confirms that goodness plays a dual developmental role: it is a product of formation (Spirit-formed character) and an agent of formation (the good person enables the formation of others — Q&A-136). The relationship to suffering deepens this: suffering is not incidental but a context in which goodness is deepened, revealed, tested, and even produced through confrontation with its absence (Q&A-133). T5.7 closes formally — no somatic deposit evidenced. The eschatological trajectory is present but underdeveloped in the data (Q&A-138-139).

findings.session_b_note: Yes — fundamentally. Love cannot be formed in isolation: it requires a beloved to be directed toward. The community formation of love (Joh 13:34 — 'love one another'; filadelfia cultivated together; training in Tit 2:4 within a community context) is inherently relational. The primary formation-by-others: reception of divine love as the enabling condition (1Jo 4:19) — God's action toward the person is the formative ground. The community of mutual love (1Pe 1:22 — 'sincere brotherly love' developed through shared obedience) is a communal-formation context. Love cannot be a solo formation project — it requires the other's presence, action, and response. The relational structure of love (always toward another) makes community the necessary formation context.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-005: Love's formation operates through a multi-layered process in the data. The primary pathway is receptive: divine love received (1Jo 4:19) → Spirit infusion (Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22) → heart-reception → soul-…
findings.finding_value: Love's formation operates through a multi-layered process in the data. The primary pathway is receptive: divine love received (1Jo 4:19) → Spirit infusion (Rom 5:5, Gal 5:22) → heart-reception → soul-response → community expression. Secondary pathways: obedience → soul purification → sincere love (1Pe 1:22); forgiveness received → love generated (Luk 7:47 — via SD-020); training within community (Tit 2:4). Love can grow (1Th 3:12) and increase through the Lord's action. Its reversibility is asymmetric: divine love is irreversible by nature (Jer 31:3 — everlasting; Lam 3:22 — never ceasing); human love is subject to redirection through competing love-allegiances (2Ti 4:10 — Demas). The eschatological trajectory is toward perfection and direct knowledge: partial now (mediated by community, neighbour-teaching), moving toward fullness (perfect love casting out fear — 1Jo 4:18; direct divine knowledge — Jer 31:34; pleasures forevermore — Psa 16:11). Formation requires community — love cannot be formed in isolation; it requires both the divine giver and the human community as the formation context.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-013: Formation in T5 operates through the same faculties identified in T3, producing their development. Memory is formed through the covenantal story — Israel's memory of God's love (Jer 2:2 — 'I remember …
findings.finding_value: Formation in T5 operates through the same faculties identified in T3, producing their development. Memory is formed through the covenantal story — Israel's memory of God's love (Jer 2:2 — 'I remember the devotion of your youth') is the ground for love's formation in both directions; formation requires knowing the love-history. Imagination is formed through eschatological vision: the forward-projection of love's fullness (Psa 27:13, Jer 31:34) orients present formation toward its goal. Identity formation is the T3.10/T5 overlap: being-named-beloved (Mat 3:17, Rom 1:7) is the formation's constitutive moment — identity received through love is the ground from which love-acts are exercised. The relational capacity faculty (T3.11) is the faculty that formation produces: the formation process (Spirit infusion, obedience-purification, training) produces a person with increasing relational capacity for love's three directional axes. The community's role in formation (Q&A-097) corresponds to the relational capacity faculty's communal engagement: the faculty cannot develop in isolation because love cannot exist without a beloved.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-016: The relational interface structure and the formation process are interdependent: the formation process is directed toward equipping the person for love's three relational axes, and the relational axes…
findings.finding_value: The relational interface structure and the formation process are interdependent: the formation process is directed toward equipping the person for love's three relational axes, and the relational axes are the context in which formation occurs. GOD→HUMAN axis as formation ground: divine love received (1Jo 4:19) is the formative act that establishes the person's capacity for all subsequent love — receiving is formation's enabling event. HUMAN→GOD axis as formation goal: total inner mobilisation (Mat 22:37 — all heart, soul, mind) is the fully formed love toward God; partial mobilisation marks love still in formation. HUMAN→HUMAN axis as formation context: community (1Pe 1:22, Tit 2:4) is both the goal-state (mutual love as community identity — Joh 13:35) and the formation context (love formed through exercising love within community). The reversibility asymmetry (divine love irreversible; human love subject to redirection) maps onto the axis structure: the GOD→HUMAN axis is the stable ground; the HUMAN→GOD and HUMAN→HUMAN axes are the formation-dependent expressions. Formation deepens the second and third axes; the first axis does not depend on formation.

findings.finding_value: Reading T5 as a whole reveals mercy's formative character: it is not static but inherently developmental and generative. The T5 synthesis: mercy produces dual transformation (objective condition + subjective orientation simultaneously); it moves persons through named inner-state sequences (at least four distinct sequences, Q&A-128); its mechanism is always specific, embodied, and costly; suffering is both the context that generates mercy-seeking and the formation-medium through which mercy-capacity deepens (Q&A-135); mercy functions as the first and foundational inner garment in the character formation sequence (Q&A-138); and mercy has an eschatological trajectory (future fullness in which the mercy-relationship is complete and permanent). T5.7 closed (no constitutional body deposit). The overarching T5 finding: mercy is a characteristic that is received, then forms the person into one who can receive it more deeply and extend it more genuinely — it has an inherent developmental arc.

findings.finding_value: T5 as a whole establishes contrition's formative logic: it is a threshold event that is not an end-state but a passage. The sequence (crushing → contrite posture → divine reviving → restored inner being) shows that the formation contrition produces is not the settling into permanent brokenness but the emergence of a character shaped by repeated breaking-and-reviving. The mechanism is dissolution-through-encounter — the inner being's self-protective structures dissolved by a reality it cannot absorb without being changed. Contrition functions as the recurring inner reset in the sanctification arc, preventing the accumulation of pride and self-sufficiency. T5.7 closes formally (no body deposit), which confirms that contrition's formative work is entirely inner-constitutional, not somatic-residual. The eschatological trajectory (T5.6) points forward but is underdeveloped in the verse evidence — the data indicates contrition is oriented toward joy and revival but does not name a final eschatological fullness.

The formation sequence (volitional alignment → habitual participation → constitutional fixing) runs from free choice to constrained character, meaning the initial choice of fellowship objects is made at maximum freedom and progressively constrains freedom as character forms. Two distinct formative mechanisms operate: participatory transfer (habituation producing conformity — gradual) and wound-as-cleansing (somatic event producing inner purification — acute). The eschatological trajectory (T5.6) is explicit in 2Pe 1:4 — fellowship is oriented toward divine nature participation as its telos.

The five-mode structure (T1) generates two distinct formation mechanisms in T5: participatory-transfer (companionship → habituation → character) and wound-as-cleansing (suffering → inner purification). T1's most radical mode (ontological, 2Pe 1:4) is T5's eschatological telos (divine nature participation as the formation endpoint).

T4's scope-narrows-as-depth-increases finding is T5's formation telos: the deepest fellowship (divine nature participation — 2Pe 1:4) is also the narrowest in scope and the furthest eschatological endpoint.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-023-005: T5 produces three inter-related formation findings. First, transformation is evidenced in both modes simultaneously (Luke 15:20-24 — the father's compassion produces condition-change in the son's stan…
findings.finding_value: T5 produces three inter-related formation findings. First, transformation is evidenced in both modes simultaneously (Luke 15:20-24 — the father's compassion produces condition-change in the son's standing AND orientation-change in his reception of identity). Second, the formative cycle is self-reinforcing: the after-state of compassion-received feeds back into the before-state of compassion-readiness in the future — the person who has received compassion becomes more capable of extending it. Third, compassion plays a dual role in the sanctification arc: it is simultaneously the character target being formed (the person becoming compassionate over time) and the motivational ground that makes the formative relationship survivable through failure and return. Matthew 18:27 introduces the most critical formative warning: received compassion can be forfeited by failure to extend it — compassion is not a permanently possessed gift but a participatory moral framework. Three distinct mechanisms of change operate across contexts: encounter/sudden (splanchnizō — the moment of being moved), covenantal-sustaining/gradual (chesed — the steady faithfulness over time), and participatory-ontological (2Pe 1:4 pattern — sharing in what God is). T5.7 is formally closed: no body deposit established. All four relationships between suffering and compassion are evidenced — suffering reveals, tests, deepens, and produces compassion.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-005: T5 produces the richest formation account of any characteristic in the review set. Five mechanisms of change are distinguished: encounter (specific relational event — Luk 1:28, Ruth 2:10), spirit-outp…
findings.finding_value: T5 produces the richest formation account of any characteristic in the review set. Five mechanisms of change are distinguished: encounter (specific relational event — Luk 1:28, Ruth 2:10), spirit-outpouring (Zec 12:10), word (Act 20:32 — grace operating through the proclaimed word), inference (Rom 8:32 — cognitive reasoning from the supreme grace-event to present assurance), and mediated-transformation (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving — Eph 4:32, SD030). Five distinct mechanisms for a single characteristic is unique in the programme data. The creaturely recognition response (fear → mourning → prostration) is confirmed as a consistent transitional state in all grace-sequences across different evidential contexts — not incidental detail but structural feature. Suffering's relationship to grace is precisely distinguished: grace inhabits suffering rather than suffering producing grace (2Cor 12:9 — weakness as theatre of grace, not as generator of grace). The reversibility question (T5.1 P2) is the most significant gap: not fully resolved. The eschatological trajectory (T5.6) is evidenced through Eph 2:7 ("the immeasurable riches of his grace in the coming ages") and charitoō's perfect-passive form (completed state with continuing effect). T2.8 remains open; T5.7 is formally left open accordingly.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — the covenant vocabulary is among the most eschatologically directed in the programme. (1) The "eternal covenant" (Heb 13:20 — OBS-034-074): the covenant is eternal in quality — it does not end at death or history's close but extends into the eternal. The resurrection of Christ "by the blood of the eternal covenant" frames the covenant as the mechanism of eschatological life. (2) New name, new song, new Jerusalem (777-003 — OBS-034-063): the kainos vocabulary in Revelation extends the new covenant's newness into the final eschatological realities — new heaven and earth (Rev 21:1), new Jerusalem (Rev 21:2), all things made new (Rev 21:5). These are the covenant's eschatological fullness: the covenant that was written on the heart (Jer 31:33) reaches its telos in the fully renewed creation. (3) Eph 2:12 — "covenants of promise" (OBS-034-060): covenant is inherently promissory — it points forward to a fullness not yet realised. The present experience of covenant is always also a foretaste of the eschatological fullness toward which the covenant moves.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-034-005: T5 as a whole reveals that covenant is the most developmentally comprehensive of all characteristics in the programme's scope — it operates across all stages of formation (entry, formation, sanctifica…
findings.finding_value: T5 as a whole reveals that covenant is the most developmentally comprehensive of all characteristics in the programme's scope — it operates across all stages of formation (entry, formation, sanctification, eschatological fullness) and all scales of time (individual, generational, covenantal-historical, eschatological). The defining T5 finding is the two-mechanism contrast (Q&A-131): the Sinai covenant uses the external-demand mechanism (discipline and instruction); the new covenant uses the internal-inscription mechanism (Spirit-writing from within). This mechanism shift is not merely methodological — it represents a change in what the covenant does to the inner person. Under the old covenant, the person is required to bring their will to the covenant; under the new, the covenant brings a transformed will to the person. T5 confirms that covenant is not a static reality but a developing one — it moves through a sequence of inner states (Q&A-128: failure → initiative → inscription → belonging → knowing), and its eschatological trajectory points toward a fullness not yet realised but already grounded in the eternal covenant (Heb 13:20).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-023: T4 reveals that the relational scope of covenant expands progressively from particular (Abraham) to national (Israel) to universal (new covenant in Christ — Q&A-119). T5 reveals that covenant moves to…
findings.finding_value: T4 reveals that the relational scope of covenant expands progressively from particular (Abraham) to national (Israel) to universal (new covenant in Christ — Q&A-119). T5 reveals that covenant moves toward eschatological fullness — from the eternal covenant (Heb 13:20 — Q&A-140) to the new creation (Rev 21:1-5 — Q&A-141). The T4 × T5 synthesis: the expanding relational scope (T4) and the eschatological trajectory (T5) are the same movement described in two registers. The Noahic covenant's universal scope (all living creatures) is the anticipation of the new covenant's universal offer and ultimately the eschatological new creation's universal scope. Covenant moves simultaneously toward wider relational inclusion (T4) and toward deeper fullness of the relationship (T5). The two trajectories are not separate but co-directional — the expansion of who is included (T4) and the deepening of what is included in (T5) are aspects of the same eschatological movement.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-034-027: T5 establishes covenant's eschatological orientation — the eternal covenant (Heb 13:20 — Q&A-140) and the new creation as the covenant's telos (Q&A-141). T7 establishes that the full vocabulary arc in…
findings.finding_value: T5 establishes covenant's eschatological orientation — the eternal covenant (Heb 13:20 — Q&A-140) and the new creation as the covenant's telos (Q&A-141). T7 establishes that the full vocabulary arc includes an eschatological dimension (Q&A-179) and that the primary anchor verse (Jer 31:33 / Heb 8:10 — Q&A-185) contains the covenant's telos within its text (the knowing of God — Jer 31:34). The T5 × T7 synthesis: the eschatological trajectory (T5) is encoded in the vocabulary and in the primary anchor verse itself (T7). The eternal covenant (T5) is named in the Hebrews vocabulary (T7 — Heb 13:20 as anchor). The eschatological knowing of God (T5 — Q&A-141: fully realised eschatological knowing) is anticipated in the primary anchor verse's promise "they shall all know me" (T7 — Q&A-185). T5's developmental trajectory finds its lexical and evidential home in the specific texts that T7 identifies as the evidential foundation. The eschatological dimension is not imposed on the data but is resident in the vocabulary arc and primary anchor verse.

findings.session_b_note: Yes — three eschatological markers: (a) Eschatological escalation: Eph 2:7 — "in the coming ages he might show the immeasurable riches of his grace in kindness toward us in Christ Jesus" [XREG: G5544, OBS-099-093]. findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-005: T5 reveals that kindness has a rich and multi-layered formative dimension. Three formation mechanisms are evidenced — Spirit-formation (organic, Gal 5:22), inscription (deliberate, Pro 3:3), and encou…
findings.finding_value: T5 reveals that kindness has a rich and multi-layered formative dimension. Three formation mechanisms are evidenced — Spirit-formation (organic, Gal 5:22), inscription (deliberate, Pro 3:3), and encounter with divine kindness (transformative, chesed corpus) — and these are not alternatives but concurrent and mutually reinforcing pathways. The formative arc produces the chasid as its telos: the person whose character is so thoroughly shaped by chesed that it has become their defining identity before God and others. This formation has an eschatological dimension: the chasid is not only preserved through life but eschatologically — Psa 16:10 ("you will not abandon my soul to Sheol") and Eph 2:7 ("in the coming ages he might show the immeasurable riches of his grace in kindness") establish that the formation kindness produces has a future that exceeds the present. Suffering does not impair kindness formation — it may deepen and reveal it (Lam 3:22 in maximum desolation; Gen 44:29/32 as sacrificial solidarity bearing suffering on behalf of another). T5's most significant intra-tier finding: the body-deposit question closes (T5.7 N — no deposit) but this does not diminish kindness's formative depth — the covenantal-formative transmission across generations (Exo 20:6 — "to a thousand generations") is more extensive than biological transmission would be, reaching all who love God and keep his commandments regardless of biological lineage.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-016: T2 and T5 together reveal the complete formation story for kindness. T2 identifies the target — heart-level character formation as the constitutional site where kindness is deposited and inscribed. T5…
findings.finding_value: T2 and T5 together reveal the complete formation story for kindness. T2 identifies the target — heart-level character formation as the constitutional site where kindness is deposited and inscribed. T5 identifies the mechanisms — Spirit-formation, inscription, and encounter — and the trajectory — from initial reception through formation to chasid identity and eschatological preservation. The T2 finding that no body-deposit exists (T2.8) is structurally consistent with T5's finding that the three formation mechanisms are non-biological: Spirit-formation, inscription, and encounter are all constitutional (spirit/heart level) or relational (encounter), not somatic. The T2 origin finding (triple origin: divine character → Spirit-mediated → humanly formed) maps onto T5's mechanism finding (encounter → inscription → organic Spirit-production) as the same formation process described from different angles — T2 asks where it comes from; T5 asks how it gets there. The eschatological dimension in T5 (the chasid is preserved beyond death) connects with the constitutional permanence finding of T2: a Spirit-formed heart-inscribed character does not dissolve with the body because it was never primarily a body-level deposit.

findings.finding_value: T4's relational circuit and T5's formation pathway are mutually reinforcing at a structural level. The T4 finding that human giving of kindness is grounded in received divine kindness (Eph 4:32 — Q&A-067) is also the primary T5 formation mechanism in its encounter mode: the encounter with divine chesed in the relational interface (T4 divine-to-human direction) is itself the formative encounter (T5 encounter mechanism) that produces the chasid. The T4 and T5 circuits are therefore not two separate processes but the same process described relationally (T4) and formationally (T5). The T5 finding that suffering does not impair kindness formation connects with T4's communal interface finding (Moses's intercession — Q&A-069): the most powerful intercessory kindness in the evidence (Moses at Num 14:19) occurs in the context of Israel's total failure — it is kindness formation under maximum covenant-crisis. The T5 eschatological trajectory finding (Eph 2:7; Psa 16:10) is the T4 divine-to-human direction extended beyond the present age: divine chesed toward the human person does not terminate at death but is eschatologically guaranteed — the T4 interface opens into eternity.

findings.finding_value: T5's formation mechanisms and T6's structural relationships interact at the level of what each characteristic in the co-occurrence cluster contributes to kindness formation. The T6 finding that kindness consistently co-occurs with faithfulness, patience, humility, and compassion maps onto T5's chasid formation arc: each of these co-occurring characteristics is also part of the formation process — faithfulness is what makes the chasid reliable over time (formation dimension); patience is what makes kindness sustainable under provocation (T5 suffering connection); humility is what prevents the chasid's identity from becoming pride (T5 formation outcome that avoids the structural opposite). The T5 formation mechanisms (Spirit-formation, inscription, encounter) all produce not just kindness in isolation but kindness in its relational cluster — the Spirit produces the full fruit (Gal 5:22: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness) not one element at a time. T5's eschatological trajectory (Eph 2:7 — immeasurable future display of kindness in Christ) is the T6 causal chain extended to its ultimate end: the causal propagation of kindness through the covenant community reaches its telos in the eschatological display of divine kindness in Christ.

findings.finding_value: T5's formation findings are directly grounded in T7's lexical evidence in a specific way: the three formation mechanisms (Spirit-formation, inscription, encounter) each correspond to a specific textual cluster in the chesed corpus. Spirit-formation is the NT Greek evidence (Gal 5:22 — chrēstotēs as fruit of the Spirit); inscription is Pro 3:3 (chesed written on the heart — the clearest constitutional formation text); encounter is the Psalms lament/praise corpus (the psalmist encountering God's chesed in distress and being transformed). T7's literary finding that kindness appears across all major literary forms (lament, praise, narrative, instruction, argument) is the T5 formation diversity mapped onto literary genre — the formation occurs in all contexts and genres, not only in instructional texts. T7's most useful human science framework (developmental psychology / attachment theory) illuminates T5's formation arc: the chasid formation trajectory maps onto attachment theory's "secure attachment → exploration → resilience" pattern — the person who has received divine chesed as secure attachment base (Psa 23:4) is equipped to explore and sustain relational kindness toward others (T4 giving) and to withstand suffering without losing kindness (T5 suffering finding).

findings.finding_value: T5 as a whole reveals that this characteristic has an eschatological orientation as its formative telos. The formation arc moves from constitutive endowment (Spirit and wisdom given to form inner-being capacity) through sustained covenantal narrative (the memory of received giving as formation environment) through suffering-testing (revealing whether inner-being giving is genuine) toward eschatological fullness ("oaks of righteousness," total communal transformation). The mechanisms are plural and context-specific — encounter (covenantal), gradual formation (endowing), sovereign reversal (eschatological) — revealing that formation is not a single pathway but a multi-modal process. The suffering relation is analytically significant: the characteristic is suffering-tested (revealed in human direction) and suffering-responsive (triggered in divine direction), showing that suffering is not incidental to the formation process but an integral context. T5.7 closes formally — no constitutional body deposit. What T5 reveals as a whole: faithfulness-as-giving is constitutively developmental — its present forms anticipate and move toward a fullness that is not yet fully realised. Every giving is, in some sense, an eschatological act: it participates in the pattern of divine giving that is moving toward total, permanent, communal transformation.

findings.finding_value: The working description of the characteristic (T1.2.3, Q&A-018) — faithfulness as an inner-being quality that enacts commitments, orientations, and compassions through giving — is directly illuminated by T5's formation account. The working description names a state of the person; T5 reveals how that state is produced and where it is oriented. Specifically: the sustained inner-being effects (T1.6: trust, praise orientation, responsiveness, cognitive formation) are precisely the formation arc outcomes of T5. Sustained covenantal giving produces identity as recipients of promise (T5.5); endowing giving constitutes cognitive capacity (T5.3); eschatological giving produces the endpoint state of "oaks of righteousness" (T5.6). What this pair reveals: the working definition of the characteristic is not a static description but an arc description — it names the person being formed toward a fullness that is not yet complete. The characteristic is definitionally developmental.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-016: The relational interfaces (T4 — divine-initiative, human-responsive, covenantal scope) and the formation arc (T5 — constitutive endowment, sustained narrative, eschatological orientation) reveal that …
findings.finding_value: The relational interfaces (T4 — divine-initiative, human-responsive, covenantal scope) and the formation arc (T5 — constitutive endowment, sustained narrative, eschatological orientation) reveal that formation happens through relational interfaces. The God-to-human interface is the channel through which constitutive formation occurs (Spirit given, wisdom deposited — T5.5). The human-to-God interface is both the goal of formation (glory-giving as the proper orientation of the formed person) and a constituent of the formation process (practising glory-giving forms the person who gives glory). What this pair reveals: formation is not an individual inner process — it is a relational event. The person is not formed in isolation from God and others; they are formed through the giving and receiving that constitutes the relational interfaces. The formation arc (T5) is the temporal dimension of the relational structure (T4): what the interfaces do over time is formation.

findings.finding_value: The formation arc (T5 — constitutive endowment → sustained covenantal narrative → suffering-testing → eschatological fullness) and the structural position (T6 — hub producing worship/hope/wisdom, produced by love/trust/compassion, connecting characteristic across all five dimensions) reveal that the formation arc is itself a structural arc through the inner-being landscape. Formation through this characteristic is formation through the relational network it occupies: the person is formed through the sequence of receiving love (R103) → receiving covenantal giving (R060) → receiving wisdom (R166) → expressing worship (R121) → approaching eschatological fullness. The characteristic is not only a hub in a synchronic sense (connected to many others at any moment) but in a diachronic sense (the formation arc moves through the relational network over time). What this pair reveals: the structural landscape is also a formation pathway. The hub position of R060 in the inner-being landscape is simultaneously a hub in the formation trajectory.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-060-020: The formation arc (T5 — developmental, eschatologically oriented, suffering-tested) and the methodological analysis (T7 — virtue ethics illuminates, diverges on received-constitutive character; Hos 11…
findings.finding_value: The formation arc (T5 — developmental, eschatologically oriented, suffering-tested) and the methodological analysis (T7 — virtue ethics illuminates, diverges on received-constitutive character; Hos 11:8 as primary anchor) produce a pointed finding. The virtue ethics framework (T7.3.2) illuminates the formation arc well — disposition formed through repeated enacted commitment toward stable character — but diverges at the key point: virtue ethics assumes the person generates virtue through practice, while the biblical account places constitutive divine giving (Spirit, wisdom) as the prior condition of formative capacity (T5.5, T2.1). The divergence maps exactly onto the T5 finding that formation is constitutively dependent on received divine giving. Hos 11:8 as primary anchor (T7.2.5) is also the key verse for the formation arc: divine compassion overriding judicial logic is itself a formative act — it preserves the relational context within which human formation can continue. What this pair reveals: the evidential and methodological analysis (T7) independently identifies the same structural priority that the formation analysis (T5) finds: the constitutive primacy of divine giving as the ground of human formation.

Yes. Two trajectories. For hatred of God: Psa 81:15: "those who hate the Lord would cringe toward him, and their fate would last forever" — the inner disposition of hatred toward God, sustained to the end, produces a permanent relational consequence. The eschatological horizon reveals what the hatred was always moving toward. For righteous hatred: when evil is finally eliminated, the hatred directed at it will have served its complete purpose — the righteous hatred is eschatologically oriented toward its own completion.

Two trajectories. For the contemner: Num 14:23: "none of those who despised me shall see it" — exclusion from the promised inheritance as the eschatological consequence. Mal 2:9: "I make you despised and abased" — the contempt is returned upon the contemner. For the despised: Isa 49:7: "kings shall see and arise; princes...shall prostrate themselves" — the one deeply despised is vindicated at the eschatological horizon. Isa 60:14: those who despised shall bow before Zion.

The most concentrated eschatological evidence in M06. Dan 12:2: "some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt (de.ra.on)" — the abhorrence becomes a permanent final condition for those who rebel. Isa 66:24: "they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh" — naming those who rebelled as a permanent eschatological reality. The characteristic reaches its fullest eschatological expression when the moral verdict of history is rendered permanent.

Trajectory is removal. Isa 29:20: "the ruthless shall come to nothing." Isa 13:11: "I will lay low the pompous pride of the ruthless." Job 27:13: "the heritage that oppressors receive from the Almighty" — the eschatological portion of the ruthless is judgment and removal. The characteristic does not move toward fullness; it is eliminated.

The most extensive and definitive eschatological removal of any characteristic in M06. Isa 25:8: "the reproach of his people he will take away from all the earth" — comprehensive and eschatological. Isa 54:4: "you will remember no more" — not merely removed but forgotten. Eze 36:15: "I will not let you hear anymore the reproach of the nations" — permanently silenced. Joe 2:19: "I will no more make you a reproach among the nations." Dan 12:2: the permanent shame and everlasting contempt (cher.pah) names the eschatological condition of the unrighteous — while everlasting life is the eschatological condition of the righteous. The eschatological future for M06-E is the complete and permanent removal of the condition from those who bore it unjustly, and the permanent establishment of the condition for those who caused it.

The adversary structure moves toward its own defeat. Job 22:20: "our adversaries are cut off." 1Pe 5:8's cosmic adversary has a terminus. The eschatological trajectory is the defeat and removal of all adversarial opposition — the characteristic that generated urgency and appeal ceases when the adversary is finally defeated.

God's judgment of the nations' malice (Eze 25:6-7, 25:15-17, 36:5-7) is the eschatological response. The "never-ending enmity" of Eze 25:15 meets divine judgment that ends it. The characteristic that claimed perpetuity is brought to nothing.

All seven sub-groups evidence eschatological orientation (see T0.2.3 above for sub-group detail). The cluster's eschatological content varies: love is permanent (M05-A — 1Cor 13:8 — Group 1542); compassion gathers the exiled in a great eschatological restoration (M05-B — Isa 54:7 — Group 1596); mercy is awaited at the last day (M05-C — Jude 21 — Group 1632); goodness moves toward completion and inherits the "good things to come" (M05-D — Heb 10:1 — Group 1099; Phili 1:6 — Group 1098); gentleness inherits the earth and is grounded in the Lord's nearness (M05-E — Mat 5:5 — Group 1261; Phili 4:5 — Group 1103); comfort is eternal (M05-F — 2Th 2:16 — Group 3074; Mat 5:4 — Group 602); fellowship participates in eschatological glory and inheritance (M05-G — 1Pe 5:1 — Group 1057; Act 20:32 — Group 2849). The cluster as a whole is eschatologically constituted — its characteristics are not only present practices but forward-pointing participations in what will be completed and revealed.

**[A1 — God Righteousness]** Yes — "to bring in everlasting righteousness" (Dan 9:24, VSG M26-A1-007); the eschatological acclamations of divine righteousness in Revelation (Rev 15:3–4; 16:5; 16:7; 19:2, VSG M26-A1-002: "just and true are your ways"; "your judgments are true and just"). God's righteousness is the standard by which the eschatological judgment is executed and the basis of the eternal order that follows.

**[A2 — Human Righteousness]** Yes — "the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will award to me on that day" (2Ti 4:8, VSG M26-A2-001). "The fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints" (Rev 19:8) — the accumulated righteousness of the saints is their eschatological identity and adornment. "In righteousness you shall be established... far from oppression, for you shall not fear" (Isa 54:14, VSG M26-A2-013) — the eschatological security of the righteous is the fullness of what righteousness promises but only partly delivers in the present order.

**[C — Justification]** Yes — "heirs according to the hope of eternal life" (Tit 3:7). The heir-status established by justification is oriented toward its eschatological fullness: inheritance, eternal life, the kingdom. Justification in the present is the first-fruits of the eschatological verdict that will be publicly declared at the final judgment.

**[D — Avenging Justice]** Yes — the eschatological cry of the martyrs (Rev 6:10, VSG 944-001) and the eschatological execution of divine justice in Rev 19:2 (VSG 944-002) are the fullest expressions of D in the cluster. Avenging justice reaches its fullness at the eschatological judgment when all accumulated injustice is finally addressed.

**[E — Condemnation]** Yes — the "punishment of eternal destruction" (2Th 1:9, VSG 949-001) and the "eternal fire" (Jude 7, VSG 949-001) locate the fullness of condemnation in the eschatological future. Condemnation in the present is a preview and warning; its fullness is at the final judgment.

**[F — Moral Reckoning]** Yes — "the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us" (Rom 8:18, VSG 3410-001). The reckoning faculty is explicitly eschatologically oriented: the act of weighing present suffering against future glory is an act of inner eschatological orientation. The faculty is exercised in the present toward what is coming.

**[G — Structural Opposites]** Yes — Rev 22:11 (VSG M26-G): "let the evildoer still do evil, and the filthy still be filthy, and the righteous still do right, and the holy still be holy." The eschatological crystallisation of moral identity — wickedness reaches its terminus in permanent exclusion from the new order.

**[CLUSTER — T5.6]** E. Every sub-group in M26 has an eschatological trajectory. This is one of the most consistently eschatological clusters in the programme. The pattern: God's righteousness is the standard of the eschatological judgment and the eternal order (A1); human righteousness reaches its fullness in the bride's garment and the crown (A2); justification's heir-status reaches its fullness in inheritance (C); avenging justice reaches its fullness in the final divine reckoning of all injustice (D); condemnation reaches its fullness in eternal punishment (E); the reckoning faculty's comparative weighing reaches its fullness when the glory that is to be revealed becomes present reality (F); wickedness reaches its terminus in permanent exclusion (G). The cluster is oriented throughout toward a final state in which all the partial and temporary modes of righteousness in this age give way to the complete and permanent.

---

**Cross-cluster finding 7 — Pervasive eschatological orientation**
Every sub-group in M26 has an eschatological trajectory (T5.6 confirmed). The cluster as a whole is eschatologically oriented to an unusual degree. The present experience of righteousness in every mode (declared, practiced, reckoned, cried for, freed from condemnation) is consistently presented as anticipatory — a first-fruits of the fullness that is coming. M26 may be the most eschatologically oriented cluster in the programme to this point.
