findings.finding_value: The present experience of reverential fear of God (M01-A) anticipates the eschatological state in which that fear is universal (Rev 15:4: "fearing the Lord portrayed as the universal, inevitable response to his holiness and revealed righteous acts" — every creature responding as the God-fearer now does in part). The present partial and contested experience of the reverential posture anticipates a future uncontested, universal, perfected version of the same posture.

The present experience of deliverance from anxiety (Psa 34:4; Isa 12:2) anticipates the fullness in which perfect love has entirely expelled fear of punishment (1Jo 4:18). The partial deliverances the verse evidence documents are provisional forms of the final state in which no fear of condemnation remains.

Each present experience of ordered fear anticipates the fullness of that fear's eschatological form. Each present deliverance from disordered fear anticipates the fullness of that deliverance. The cluster's present evidence is consistently anticipatory — it describes a movement whose destination is clear.

The present experience of divine anger (whether as discipline of covenant people or as judgment of nations) anticipates the final day when all outstanding moral accounts are settled (Rev 14:10; 16:19; 19:15). The present is the partial and provisional; the eschatological is the total and final. The believer's deliverance from wrath in the present (1Th 1:10) anticipates the complete deliverance at Christ's coming (1Th 5:9).

God's present jealous passion for his people and city (Zec 1:14; Zec 8:2 / M02-E-VCG-02) anticipates the fullness of the kingdom where his exclusive claim is never violated. The present jealousy, which still arises because rivals still exist, anticipates a future where the jealousy is permanently and unreservedly satisfied.

The present experience of grief anticipates that the new creation will be characterised by the complete absence of every form of M03's register: no weeping, no mourning, no crying, no pain, no groaning, no sorrow (the catalogue of Rev 21:4). The present experience of grief is therefore not without eschatological meaning — it is the inner condition of those who know what is missing from the not-yet. Exile-grief (Psa 137:1 — M03-A-VCG-03) anticipates restoration; sighing anticipates everlasting joy; creation's groan anticipates redemption. Grief is the eschatological condition that knows it is not yet home.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Present exultation in God's salvation (Psa 35:9; Isa 61:10; Hab 3:18) anticipates: (1) the completion of all partial deliverances in a final, total rescue; (2) the mutual exultation of God and his people ("your God will exult over you" — Zep 3:17; "I will rejoice in Jerusalem" — Isa 65:19) at the fullest expression of the covenant; (3) the extension of exultation to the whole created order (Psa 96:11; 97:1; Isa 49:13) in cosmic celebration of God's reign. Present exultation is a first-fruits of an eschatological harvest.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Present Joy is consistently characterised as partial and anticipatory: Joh 16:22 (sorrow now, hearts will rejoice when Jesus is seen again — present sorrow is the birth-pangs of future Joy); Psa 51:12 (restore to me Joy — present lack as the pointer to promised fullness); 1Pe 1:6–8 (rejoicing in salvation being revealed — present partial experience of an inheritance fully coming). The present experience of Joy functions as a first-fruits: genuine, real, but not yet at its promised maximum. The NT's emphasis on Joy's fullness (pleron — full, filled, complete) throughout the Johannine corpus confirms this: present joy is real but moves toward completion.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Present Suffering-Joy anticipates: (1) the full replacement of suffering by unqualified joy (1Pe 4:13 — "rejoice and be glad" at revelation, without the "insofar as suffering" qualification); (2) the full revelation of the glory that present joy is already filled with (1Pe 1:8's "filled with glory" → fully manifest at the revelation); (3) the communal eschatological celebration of the Lamb's marriage (Rev 19:7) — the final convergence of all suffering-joy into an unqualified corporate rejoicing. Present Suffering-Joy is partial, coexisting with grief (1Pe 1:6); future fullness is unqualified, permanent, and communal.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Present Gladness anticipates: (1) the complete vindication of the evaluative faculty — when creation's "very good" (Gen 1:31) is fully restored; (2) the complete fulfilment of all God's good promises (the trajectory of Jos 21:45 applied eschatologically); (3) the blessedness of the fully declared-righteous before God (the makarismos trajectory). Present Gladness in God's character-goodness (ki-tov) is a present experience of what will be the permanent, uninterrupted inner state of those who know him.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Present Delight in God's law (Psa 119; Psa 1) anticipates the eschatological state where law is fully internalized (Jer 31:33 — new covenant writing on the heart) and obedience is no longer law-external but perfectly law-internal (Psa 40:8 fulfilled completely). Present Delight in the Lord (Psa 37:4; Isa 58:14) anticipates the eschatological state of Job 22:26 where Delight in the Almighty is uninterrupted and fully satisfying. Present divine Delight in the person (Psa 18:19; Isa 62:4) anticipates the eschatological community named "My Delight Is in Her" — where God's Delight toward his people is the permanent, publicly declared, eternally sustaining reality.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Present Pleasure in God's beauty (Psa 27:4 — gazing in the temple) anticipates the fullness of Psa 16:11's "pleasures forevermore" when God's presence is unmediated and permanent. The present ni.cho.ach worship-Pleasure relationship anticipates Eze 20:41's final acceptance. Present wisdom-Pleasure (Pro 2:10; 3:17) anticipates a future in which the whole person and community inhabit wisdom's pleasantness completely. The river of delights (Psa 36:8) anticipates the eschatological river of life.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Present Wonder at God's acts in history (VCG-01) anticipates the eschatological fullness of Isa 29:14's "wonder upon wonder" when God's acts will so completely exceed human comprehension that even the wise will be rendered speechless. Present Wonder at the Wonderful Counselor (Isa 9:6) anticipates the fullness of encounter with him whose character is inherently wonder-inducing. Present epistemological humility (Job 42:3; Psa 131:1) anticipates the eschatological state of perfect knowing before the fully-revealed God (1Cor 13:12 — "then I shall know fully, even as I have been fully known" — not in corpus but anticipated by the Wonder-humility posture).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The present experiences across the seven anticipate their eschatological fullness through a consistent pattern: each present form is a **first-fruits of a harvest not yet arrived**. Joy's present form (rejoicing in God's salvation) anticipates the "everlasting joy" of Isa 51:11; Suffering-Joy's present form (Spirit-produced exultation amid grief) anticipates the unqualified glory-joy of 1Pe 4:13; Wonder's present form (arrested astonishment at God's acts) anticipates the "wonder upon wonder" of Isa 29:14 when the wise are rendered speechless; Delight's present form (Psa 37:4's restructured desires) anticipates Job 22:26's uninterrupted Delight in the Almighty; Pleasure's present form (gazing on God's beauty in the temple — Psa 27:4) anticipates the face-to-face beatific encounter of the eschatological age (Rev 22:4 — not in corpus but anticipated by the posture). The cluster presents the seven characteristics as genuine present realities that are simultaneously partial, anticipatory, and forward-leaning. Present M04 characteristics are not shadows but genuine first-fruits.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The present experience of shame anticipates two futures, in tension. (1) In the unjust-wound register: present shame anticipates its permanent removal and transformation into honour, praise, and double portion. The shame is real and painful now; its future is its opposite. (2) In the corrective register: present shame before God's holiness anticipates the fullness of knowing God's design — shame is the entry-point to a fuller relationship, not the permanent condition. Eze 43:11: when Israel is ashamed, the full design is disclosed — the future fullness (knowing the design, carrying it out) is what shame is the gateway toward. The eschatological direction of CHAR-1 is therefore toward its own resolution and replacement, not its perpetuation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, strongly. (1) The Day-of-the-Lord material (Isa 2:9-17; 13:11) points toward eschatological completion. (2) 1Cor 15:43 — body sown in dishonor, raised in glory — is the eschatological resolution of CHAR-2 at the individual level. (3) Hab 2:16 — "utter shame will come upon your glory" — is directed eschatologically: God's cup of judgment will finally execute the complete reversal of all proud human standing.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — The structural-dishonour mode (VCG-02) points toward its own eschatological resolution: 2Ti 2:20's vessel for dishonorable use is implicitly oriented toward the possibility of cleansing (2:21 context). Rom 9:21's potter-and-clay raises the deepest eschatological question: sovereign assignment of dishonour-standings as a condition of creaturely existence, and whether eschatological transformation re-assigns those standings.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — Rev 16:15 frames CHAR-4's proper functioning as oriented toward the moment of Christ's coming: the one who "stays awake, keeping his garments on" avoids the shame of exposure at that moment. The eschatological fullness is the state in which moral vigilance has been sustained and the shameful has been renounced throughout — so that at Christ's coming no exposure occurs. CHAR-4's eschatological trajectory is toward the full activation and correct calibration of the moral-evaluative conscience.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. Act 4:11 (the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone) is the paradigmatic eschatological statement of CHAR-5's reversal. 1Cor 1:28 (God choosing the despised to nullify things that are) is the eschatological programme: the world's contempt-verdicts are being overturned, and this overturning will be completed in the eschaton. The present experience of CHAR-5 anticipates its final reversal — shame from contempt is a temporary condition oriented toward the vindicating re-worth-assignment of God.

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — Psa 73:13's lament — maintained innocence apparently futile — is resolved in its wider context by the sanctuary encounter and the eschatological vindication of the righteous. The present experience of CHAR-6 (maintained innocence under suffering) anticipates its eschatological vindication: the person who maintains moral integrity will find it vindicated when "their end" is seen clearly (Psa 73:17). The eschatological fullness is the state in which innocence's protective function is fully confirmed and the wicked's apparently successful rejection of it is finally judged.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — At the cluster level, M07's eschatological trajectory is toward the permanent resolution of all shame-producing conditions and the full restoration of inner standing, worth, and innocence that shame has violated. The most explicit statements: Char 1 (Isa 54:4; 61:7; Joe 2:26-27 — shame removed, replaced by double portion and everlasting joy; Isa 45:17 — never put to shame to all eternity), Char 2 (1Cor 15:43 — dishonored body raised in glory), Chars 3 and 5 (God's final correct worth-assignment overturning all contempt-verdicts), Char 4 (Rev 16:15 — the vigilant maintaining of conscience toward Christ's coming), Char 6 (Psa 73's lament resolved in the sanctuary pointing toward final vindication). Cluster-level picture of the eschatological fullness: no unjust shame remains; no proud humiliation is needed because pride has been finally corrected; all worth is correctly assigned; all conscience is fully calibrated to God's standard; all contempt-verdicts are overturned; all moral integrity is vindicated. M07's eschatological orientation is the most comprehensive in the programme for the promise-density directed at a single inner-being domain.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The present experience of CHAR-1 anticipates its own reversal and judgment, not a positive future state. Isa 14:11 (vc=33988, M08-A3-VCG-02): "your pomp is brought down to Sheol, the sound of your harps; maggots are laid as a bed beneath you" — the present display of CHAR-1 (pomp, grandeur) anticipates its terminus in degradation and death. Pro 29:23 (vc=33960, M08-A4-VCG-04): "one's pride will bring him low" — the present experience of self-elevation structurally anticipates humiliation as its outcome. Isa 2:11 (vc=34089, M08-A2-VCG-01; vc=34601, M08-A3-VCG-04): "the haughty looks of man shall be brought low" — the present posture of haughty-eyed self-elevation anticipates the eschatological day when those looks will specifically be brought down. CHAR-1's present experience offers no anticipation of a positive future fullness — every eschatological trajectory evidenced in the corpus runs toward reversal, humiliation, and the establishment of God's sole exaltation in place of the creature's self-elevation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The present experience of CHAR-2 anticipates its eschatological annihilation. Mal 4:1 (vc=34107): the present arrogance ("the arrogant" who are currently calling evildoers blessed — Mal 3:15, vc=34106) anticipates the day when they become "stubble" consumed by fire. Pro 11:2 (vc=34109, M08-B-VCG-02): "when arrogance comes, disgrace follows" — the present experience of CHAR-2 structurally anticipates disgrace as its immediate trajectory. Jer 50:32 (vc=34117): "a fall with no one to restore" — the present self-willed defiance anticipates total and unrecoverable collapse.

**[CHAR-3]** E — VCG-03 present boasting anticipates the eschatological boasting before Christ (1Th 2:19; Phili 2:16) — the present relational commendation of community members is a foretaste of the eschatological presentation before the Lord. VCG-01 present boasting anticipates exposure and empty consequence (Pro 25:14: clouds and wind without rain; 1Cor 5:6: the corruption spreading). The present experience of CHAR-3 anticipates either eschatological boasting before Christ (VCG-03) or the exposure of its emptiness (VCG-01).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The present experience of CHAR-4 anticipates: (a) Epistemic deepening toward blindness: 1Ti 6:4 (vc=33925, M08-D-VCG-02) — the present inflation anticipates the terminal state of understanding nothing; (b) Judicial condemnation: 1Ti 3:6 (vc=33924) — the conceited person's present inflation anticipates the adversarial condemnation-category. (c) Communal disorder: 2Cor 12:20 (vc=33942) — the present conceit anticipates the relational collapse that Paul fears finding.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The present experience of CHAR-5 anticipates: (a) The sudden removal of the structural foundation: Isa 47:8 (vc=9563, M08-E-VCG-02): Babylon says "I shall not sit as a widow" — the present confident denial anticipates the sudden arrival of exactly what was denied ("these two things shall come to you in a moment" — context of v.9); (b) Total desolation when power is stripped: Eze 33:28 (vc=33999): the present proud might anticipates the desolation that follows its removal; (c) The exposure of structural security as false: Obd 3 (vc=65674): "who will bring me down?" — the present confident question anticipates the answer: God will.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster comparison reveals the cluster's systematic eschatological logic: M08 characteristics generate a present experience that anticipates its own reversal. The self-exaltation of CHAR-1 anticipates humbling. The defiance of CHAR-2 anticipates judgment. The self-boasting of CHAR-3 anticipates exposure. The cognitive inflation of CHAR-4 anticipates the condemnation of the devil. The self-sufficiency of CHAR-5 anticipates desolation. The cluster-synthesis: M08 characteristics are internally self-undermining eschatologically — each present expression of pride carries within it the structural anticipation of its own reversal. Pro 16:18 (M08-A1-VCG-03: "pride goes before destruction") states this as a structural law for CHAR-1, but the same logic runs through all five.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The present obedience of faith (Rom1:5; 16:26) anticipates the eschatological fullness of universal submission to Christ (Gen49:10 — all peoples; Heb5:9 — all who obey him). Every present act of will-submission to Christ is a partial and anticipatory realisation of the eschatological telos: the gathering of all peoples in willing allegiance to the one who is "Lord of all." The present household obedience (Eph6:1 — in the Lord) and the present obedience to apostolic instruction (Phili2:12 — with fear and trembling) are microcosms of the macrocosmic submission that the eschatological gathering represents.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The present experience of contrition and God's reviving (Isa57:15) anticipates a fullness in which the person's spirit and heart are permanently revived rather than cyclically broken and renewed. The reviving in Isa57:15 is a present experience of what the final resurrection-life will be constitutively: the creaturely person fully revived and dwelling with the holy God without the broken-and-revived cycle that characterises present experience.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Heb5:2's present form of the characteristic (the human high priest's metriopatheō grounded in shared weakness) anticipates the eschatological perfection in Christ who is "beset with" human weakness not merely by office but by the Incarnation itself — the fuller, more thoroughgoing identification that produces the superior priestly sympathy. The present form of the characteristic (partial, grounded in limited human self-knowledge) anticipates its fullness in the one who identifies fully with human weakness.
**[CHAR-5]** S — The evidence is silent on what present semnotēs anticipates in eschatological fullness. Prompt closed.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The present experience of willing-heartedness in offering and service (Exo35; 2Ch29:31) anticipates the eschatological fullness in which the whole community gives freely and gladly to God without the fragility that Psa51:12 evidences — the present willingness is partial and vulnerable to disruption; the eschatological fullness would be permanent and uninterruptible. Psa51:12's prayer for a divine-upheld willing spirit anticipates the eschatological state in which the willing spirit is continuously and permanently upheld rather than requiring repeated restoration.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The present experience of voluntary self-lowering (M09-A) anticipates a reversal: divine exaltation is the promised complement. The person who humbles themselves now participates in the same kenotic movement as Christ (Phili2:8) and therefore participates in the pattern of Christ's exaltation (Phili2:9 — "therefore God has highly exalted him" — outside this corpus but the structural pattern confirmed by 1Pe5:6). The present experience of creaturely lowliness (M09-B — Phili3:21 "lowly body") anticipates transformation into conformity with the glorified body — the condition of creatureliness, genuinely accepted and inhabited in humility, becomes the starting point from which glorification proceeds. The characteristic thus does not point away from the present creaturely condition but through it toward its transformation.

**[CLUSTER]** E — Each characteristic's present experience anticipates a corresponding eschatological state. Humility (CHAR-1): present voluntary self-lowering anticipates divine exaltation at the proper time (1Pe5:6) and bodily transformation (Phili3:21 — the lowly body transformed into conformity with the glorified body); participation in the kenotic movement of the Son anticipates participation in the reversal. Submission (CHAR-2): every present act of will-submission to Christ anticipates the eschatological fullness of universal submission of all peoples (Gen49:10; Rom16:26); present obedience is a microcosm of the macrocosmic gathering. Contrition (CHAR-3): present contrition and God's reviving anticipates the fullness in which spirit and heart are permanently revived rather than cyclically broken and renewed — the eschatological state makes permanent what Isa57:15 delivers episodically. Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4): the present form (Aaronic priest's metriopatheō grounded in shared weakness — Heb5:2) anticipates the superior priestly sympathy of the one who identifies fully with human weakness without being beset by it. Dignity (CHAR-5): the evidence is silent on eschatological anticipation — semnotēs is a present-ordering quality without direct eschatological trajectory in this corpus. Willing-heartedness (CHAR-6): present willing-heartedness (fragile and renewable — Psa51:12) anticipates the eschatological state in which the willing spirit is continuously and permanently upheld, requiring no further restoration.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The present experience of wilful sinning anticipates, in the corpus, either *judgment* or *forgiveness* as its eschatological resolution — there is no neutral final state. 2Pe 2:4 shows judgment as the trajectory for un-remedied sinning (the angels kept for judgment). Lev 4:35 / 2Sa 12:13 / 1Jo 2:1 (advocate with the Father) show forgiveness as the eschatological resolution for sinning that is confessed and remedied. The characteristic's present operation anticipates a final accounting — the sinning act is not closed at the moment of commission but remains open before God until either judgment or forgiveness resolves it.

**[CHAR-10]** E — 2Pe 2:14's "Accursed children!" — the present practice of enticement anticipates an eschatological verdict of divine curse; the curse-label in the present names the future judgment trajectory. The barely-escaping souls of 2Pe 2:18 who are re-captured by enticement move toward the same judgment-trajectory as the enticers if they are re-integrated into the error from which they were barely escaping. The present enticement mechanism anticipates the eschatological consequence of being fully captured rather than escaping.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The present experience of sin as universal condition anticipates two contrasted futures. For those remaining in it: Joh 8:24 — "you will die in your sins" — the present condition of being-in-sin anticipates the future of dying-in-sin as the condition's full consequence; 1Th 2:16 — the present accumulation of the measure anticipates the full measure that triggers judgment. For those freed from it: Rom 6:22 — the present fruit of sanctification anticipates eternal life as the condition's positive future; 1Cor 15:17 — "you are still in your sins" without the resurrection — conversely, the resurrection grounds the future hope of being freed from the condition permanently.

**[CHAR-12]** E — For those remaining under the enslaving power: 1Jo 5:16 — present sinning-toward-death anticipates death as the enslavement's eschatological culmination; 1Jo 3:8 — present devil-allegiance ("of the devil") anticipates the eschatological verdict that aligns the person with the devil's judgment. For those liberated from it: 1Jo 5:18 — the present protection from the evil one anticipates the permanent inability of the evil one to touch; 1Jo 3:8 — the Son of God's present destroying of the devil's works anticipates the complete destruction that removes the enslaving power's foundation.

**[CHAR-13]** E — For those whose record persists unaddressed: Hos 13:12 — the present sealed record anticipates the future reckoning (the stored record awaits its day); Exo 32:34 — the present deferred visitation anticipates the appointed day of full enforcement. For those whose record is being addressed: Jer 31:34 — the present partial experience of forgiveness anticipates the new-covenant fullness where the record is permanently erased; Dan 9:24 — the present sin-bearing anticipates the eschatological "end of sin" and the installation of everlasting righteousness. The record's present state anticipates either its eschatological enforcement or its eschatological erasure.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The OT kip.pu.rim system anticipates its own eschatological supersession: each annual Day of Atonement (Lev 23:27/28) is complete in itself yet points forward to the once-for-all atonement (Mat 26:28). For the NT believer: Eph 1:7 — "in him we have redemption, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace" — the present "we have" anticipates the eschatological fullness of riches of grace; Col 1:14 — "in whom we have redemption" — the present redemption-possession anticipates the final redemption-completeness. Act 2:38's Spirit-reception is the "deposit" of the eschatological inheritance (Eph 1:14 context — outside this corpus but implicit in the Spirit-gift).

**[CHAR-15]** E — For the community under the generational condition: Isa 64:5 — "shall we be saved?" — the present salvific uncertainty anticipates the eschatological question of whether God's cleansing will be received; Jer 8:14's doom anticipates the eschatological consequence of unresolved generational sinning. For the community promised cleansing: Eze 37:23's "I will save them and cleanse them" anticipates the eschatological fullness in which the accumulated backslidings are permanently resolved and the covenant-people identity is definitively restored.

**[CHAR-16]** E — For the unrepentant sinner: Pro 13:21 — "disaster pursues sinners" — the present pursuit of disaster anticipates the eschatological destruction; Amo 9:10 — the sinners' present presumption ("disaster shall not overtake us") anticipates the eschatological reversal (they "shall die by the sword"). For the repentant sinner: Luk 15:7/10 — the present joy in heaven over one sinner who repents anticipates the eschatological fullness of restored relationship; 1Ti 1:16 — Paul's transformation anticipates the pattern ("an example to those who were to believe in him for eternal life") of all who move from sinner-identity to life.

**[CHAR-17]** E — For the unaddressed guilt: Eze 21:23/24 — the present guilt remembered by God anticipates the eschatological day when it is "brought to remembrance... that they may be taken"; the present guilt-experience anticipates its eschatological enforcement. For the acknowledged guilt: Isa 6:7 — the present removal of Isaiah's guilt (lips touched, guilt taken away) anticipates the eschatological fullness of complete guilt-cleansing; Jer 33:8 — the future total cleansing is the eschatological fullness toward which present partial guilt-resolution points.

**[CHAR-18]** E — For the unaddressed accumulation: Gen 15:16's "not yet complete" anticipates the eschatological day when it is complete and judgment falls; Hos 13:12's "bound up and kept in store" anticipates the day when the sealed record is opened for judgment. For the addressed iniquity: Zec 3:4's "I have taken your iniquity away" anticipates Zec 3:9's single-day removal for the whole land — individual removals point toward the eschatological total removal; Isa 53:6's "the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all" anticipates the new covenant's comprehensive forgiveness (Jer 31:34).

**[CHAR-19]** E — For the unrepentant: Amos 1:3's "three and four" accumulation anticipates the eschatological day when the threshold is finally reached for all nations and individuals (Dan 8:23 — "when transgressors have reached their limit"). The present counting is the pre-eschatological accumulation toward Dan 9:24's "finish the transgression." For the repentant: Psa 32:1's blessedness of forgiven transgression anticipates Eze 37:23's eschatological state — "they shall not defile themselves anymore with any of their transgressions... and they shall be my people, and I will be their God."

**[CHAR-2]** E — The present experience of unintentional sinning and its prescribed remedy (offering → atonement → forgiveness) anticipates a future in which the knowledge-gap that makes inadvertent sinning possible is finally closed — a state in which the creature no longer sins even inadvertently because creaturely epistemic limitation is overcome. The present remedial system (Lev 4:2; Num 15:27/28) is provisional — it addresses the liability but does not eliminate the knowledge-gap that produces it. The eschatological trajectory points toward the elimination of the gap itself, not merely its remediation. The daily altar purification (Exo 29:36) pointing toward the eschatological temple purification (Eze 45:18) traces this arc: repeated provisional remedy → final comprehensive cleansing.

**[CHAR-20]** E — For the unrepentant: 2Ch 28:22's progressive deepening anticipates the eschatological endpoint of complete desolation (2Ch 30:7 — made them a desolation); the present hardening-under-distress is the pre-eschatological trajectory toward irreversible judgment. For the confessing community: Lev 26:40's honest confession anticipates Lev 26:42's covenant-restoration; Eze 39:26's secure-dwelling promise is the eschatological fullness that present confession moves toward.

**[CHAR-21]** E — For the unrepentant: 2Pe 2:12's "born to be caught and destroyed" anticipates the eschatological destruction that matches their corrupted nature; Jude 10's "destroyed by what they understand instinctively" names the present instinct-driven destruction as the eschatological pattern in miniature. For the addressed perversion: Rom 8:21's present "bondage to corruption" anticipates the eschatological "freedom of the glory of the children of God"; Eph 4:24's "put on the new self, created after the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness" anticipates the eschatological fullness of the image-likeness restored.

**[CHAR-22]** E — For the persistent unjust: 2Pe 2:9's current custody under punishment anticipates the day-of-judgment verdict; Rev 18:5's "God has remembered" anticipates the reckoning at which the heaped-high sins are adjudicated. For the addressing-injustice person: Eze 33:15's "he shall surely live" anticipates the eschatological life of the purified community (Zep 3:13 — "do no injustice"); the present act of withholding the hand from injustice (Eze 18:8) anticipates the eschatological remnant's permanent non-injustice.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The present experience of confession (naming sin, accepting indignation, trusting in God's response — Mic 7:9) anticipates a future in which the naming is completed by the divine verdict of vindication. The confession names what the person did; the future fullness is God naming what he will do — "He will bring me out to the light." The present confession is oriented toward a final state in which the sin named is not merely cancelled but superseded by the light of God's vindication. Job 33:27 — "I sinned... and it was not repaid to me" — the restored man's testimony anticipates a state in which the full justice of God's mercy (not repaying the sin) is publicly evident.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The present experience of conscience suppression (false peace, assumed innocence, moral stupor) anticipates a future reckoning that will expose what the suppressed conscience refused to surface. Jer 2:35 — the person who says "his anger has turned from me" anticipates instead the judgment that God has declared. The false peace of conscience suppression is the inverse anticipation of the real judgment: the more fully the conscience is suppressed now, the less prepared the person is for the judgment to come. Job 35:6 — "If you have sinned, what do you accomplish against him?" — Elihu's point that sin harms the sinner (not God) points toward the sinner bearing the consequence: the judgment that conscience suppression avoids facing inwardly will be faced outwardly.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The present experience of refusal to repent (continued walking in the sinful course, the sacrifice closed off, the moral record of righteous deeds erased — Eze 18:24) anticipates a future of divine reckoning without available remedy. Heb 10:26 — "there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins" — the present foreclosure of the sacrifice anticipates a future where the foreclosure becomes permanent: judgment without the provision that would have enabled forgiveness. The present refusal forecloses the future remedy: what the refusing will withholds now (the turn) is what would have opened the future (forgiveness and life); refusing the turn now anticipates a future of unaddressed moral liability before the judge.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The present experience of habitual defection (continued sinning, hardened orientation, institutional embedding, epistemic blindness) anticipates a future of confirmed consequence: Pro 13:22 (wealth redirected — what is accumulated is not kept), Pro 11:31 (amplified recompense), and the eschatological non-seeing of God (1Jo 3:6 — "never seen or known him" points toward a future of confirmed non-encounter). The present pattern anticipates a future where the present orientation is confirmed and fixed: the sinner who keeps on sinning moves toward a future in which the habitual sinning direction is definitively the person's standing before God's judgment.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The present experience of contagious sin (the community's inner orientation being reshaped away from God through the leader's authority) anticipates a future of either judgment (1Ki 14:16 — abandonment) or structural reversal (2Ki 23:15 — dismantling). The contagious sin transmission does not remain stable: it either escalates toward judgment (the Northern Kingdom's trajectory) or is reversed by counter-formation leadership (Josiah). The present transmission thus carries either the trajectory of accumulating divine consequence or the possibility of structural reversal, depending on whether a counter-formation leader emerges.

**[CHAR-8]** E — 1Ki 12:19 / 2Ch 10:19's "to this day" names the ongoing state of fracture as an unresolved wound in the covenant history. The present experience of political revolt (the ongoing broken relationship) anticipates a future in which the fracture is either confirmed as permanent or resolved through divine action. The typological direction (T0.4.1/T0.4.2) points toward the latter: the eschatological expectation of Davidic restoration as the antitype of the present revolt. The present revolt is the negative that anticipates the positive eschatological resolution.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The present experience of sinful speech anticipates: (1) For the Spirit-blasphemy form — permanent eschatological non-forgiveness (Mat 12:31); (2) For VCG-03's beast-blasphemy — divine judgment that ends the forty-two month period of permitted blasphemy (Rev 13:5 — "it was allowed to exercise authority for forty-two months" implies a terminus); (3) For addressable forms — the possibility of the reversal that 1Ti 1:13 models. The present sinful speech thus anticipates either the permanent confirmation of the unforgiven state or the transformation available through mercy.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The present experience of wickedness-as-settled-person-identity anticipates its future dissolution through internal signals already present. Pro 10:24 (VCG-06): "what the wicked dreads will come upon him" — the inner dread is a present anticipation of the future judgment the conscience cannot fully suppress. Isa 57:20-21 (VCG-02): the inner restlessness of the wicked ("like the tossing sea… no peace") is the present analogue of the complete dissolution that awaits. Job 15:20 (VCG-06): "the wicked man writhes in pain all his days" — the present inner torment is the beginning of the future judgment. The present experience of the characteristic therefore carries within itself anticipatory signals of its future termination — the characteristic is already self-consuming, already moving toward its own end, in the inner-experience of dread, want, and torment.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The present experience anticipates: (1) the deepening deterioration trajectory — 2Ti 3:13 (vc=14451 — VCG-06) shows the present "from bad to worse" as anticipating the eschatological terminus of that trajectory; (2) the evil conscience's present barrier to God — Heb 10:22 (vc=14426 — VCG-06) shows the present state of the evil conscience as anticipating its eschatological consequence (permanent separation from the holy God unless cleansed); (3) the present love of darkness — Joh 3:19 (vc=14448 — VCG-04) anticipates the eschatological settling into that preference (Mat 13:49 — separation of the evil). The present experience of the characteristic carries within it the seeds of its eschatological outcome.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The present experience of abomination anticipates: (1) the eschatological exclusion — Rev 21:27 (vc=22 — VCG-05): those who do what is detestable are excluded from the holy city; the present experience of exclusion from divine intimacy (Pro 3:32 — VCG-02) and from worship acceptability (VCG-03) anticipates this final exclusion; (2) the permanent weight of shame — Eze 44:13 (vc=66003 — VCG-04): bearing shame permanently anticipates the eschatological state where the shame-burden is not lifted; (3) the removal of abomination from the divine presence — the present divine revulsion (Pro 6:16 — VCG-05: God hates; Pro 11:1 — VCG-01: God finds it abominable) anticipates the eschatological act of exclusion. The present characteristic carries within it the seeds of its eschatological terminus.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The present experience of idolatrous abomination anticipates: (1) progressive escalation — Eze 8:13; 8:15 (VCG-05: "still greater abominations") — the present pattern of deepening anticipates its eschatological maximum; (2) divine-presence withdrawal — Eze 5:11 (vc=65969 — VCG-05): God's withdrawal from the defiled sanctuary anticipates the final eschatological separation; (3) the abomination-of-desolation event — the present historical desecrations (sanctuary defiled by idols — Jer 7:30; 32:34 — VCG-04) anticipate the eschatological desolation-event (Dan 9:27; Mat 24:15 — VCG-06). The present experience carries within it the seeds of the eschatological culmination: each act of idolatrous abomination advances the trajectory toward its maximum expression.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The present experience of iniquity as active scheming anticipates: (1) inevitable divine return of the accumulated iniquity — Psa 94:23 (VCG-03): the present accumulation will be returned as judgment; (2) the temporary nature of apparent flourishing — Psa 92:7 (VCG-03): present sprouting-like-grass anticipates permanent destruction; (3) the eventual complete collapse — Psa 36:12 (vc=38233 — VCG-04): "thrust down, unable to rise" — the present trajectory anticipates its terminus of irrecoverable ruin. The present experience of the characteristic is eschatologically loaded: each act of scheming builds toward the accumulated ruin that will be returned in full.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Present evil expressed through speech anticipates: (1) the eschatological maximum of blasphemy — the beast's sustained cosmic blasphemy (Rev 13:6 — VCG-01) as the concentrated endpoint of all human and adversarial defiant speech; present instances of blasphemous defiance participate in and anticipate this eschatological peak; (2) the eschatological reversal of false accusation — 1Pe 2:12 (vc=14377 — VCG-03): "glorify God on the day of visitation" — the false accusation's present impact is reversed in the eschatological moment when truth is established; (3) the condemnation of slander — Rom 3:8 (vc=14358 — VCG-02): "their condemnation is just" — the present slanderous misrepresentation carries within it the certain eschatological condemnation.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster reveals that the present experience of each M10b characteristic carries within it the seeds of the eschatological terminal state. Present wickedness (Char 1) anticipates the eschatological "wicked shall act wickedly" hardening. Present constitutional evil (Char 2) anticipates the "present evil age" being transcended (Gal 1:4). Present abomination (Char 3) anticipates its eschatological exclusion from the holy city (Rev 21:27). Present idolatrous abomination (Char 4) anticipates the abomination-of-desolation event (Dan 9:27 → Mat 24:15). Present iniquity-scheming (Char 5) anticipates the retributive return of accumulated iniquity (Psa 94:23). Present blasphemous speech (Char 6) anticipates the beast's concentrated cosmic blasphemy (Rev 13:6) and the population's final unrepentant state (Rev 16:21). The cluster's common eschatological anticipation: each present instance of M10b evil participates in and moves toward the same eschatological finale of elimination and exclusion.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The present experience of the defilement-state — the structured cycle of acquisition, conscience-awakening, remedy, and restoration — anticipates a future in which the need for management is no longer present: a state of unrestricted access to divine presence, without the bodily vulnerabilities of death-contact and discharge. The red-heifer provision's framing as a "sin offering" (Num 19:9) anticipates a sacrifice that resolves the defilement problem at a deeper level than the ritual can achieve. The Act 10:28 revision anticipates a community in which the relational exclusions built into the ritual system are overcome.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The present moral-inner defilement-state (in the negative form) and the present non-defilement (in the positive-inverse form of VCG-05) both anticipate the eschatological state. The present defilement anticipates exclusion from the eschatological fullness (Eph 5:5 — no inheritance; Isa 35:8 — cannot pass over the Way of Holiness). The present non-defilement anticipates inclusion in the eschatological fullness (Rev 3:4 — walk with Christ in white; Rev 14:4 — firstfruits for God and the Lamb). The eschatological fullness is the permanent, unreversible establishment of the moral-inner clean state — the completion of holiness (2Cor 7:1) that the present process of cleansing anticipates.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The present corporate/covenantal defilement-state (in the pre-exilic and exilic registers) anticipates the eschatological fullness of permanent non-defilement, restored covenant relationship, and purified sacred community. The present memory of defilement in exile (Eze 20:43 — self-loathing) anticipates the future community's humility before God in the restoration. The present defilement of land, sanctuary, and name anticipates their eschatological purification (Isa 52:1 — holy city; Zec 13:1 — cleansing fountain). The present state thus anticipates the fullness precisely through the contrast it provides: the depth of the defilement reveals the scope of the cleansing required and promised.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The present experience of expulsion and restoration anticipates an eschatological fullness of permanent wholeness — a community of persons in which no unclean spirit can inhabit, control, or defile. Each healing (Luk 6:18 — "were cured"; Act 5:16 — "all healed"; Luk 9:42 — "healed... gave him back to his father") is a present anticipation of the fullness in which the characteristic has no domain. The commissioned authority of Mat 10:1 and Mar 6:7 (VCG-03) anticipates the eschatological complete authority over all adversarial spiritual powers that the kingdom's consummation will bring.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The four present-experience anticipations point toward a common eschatological fullness through different registers. Characteristic 1 anticipates: unrestricted access to divine presence without bodily vulnerabilities; a community in which the covenantal relational exclusions of the ritual system are overcome (Act 10:28 — all persons declared clean). Characteristic 2 anticipates: permanent holiness — the completion of the present arc of cleansing (2Cor 7:1); intimate following of the Lamb without the characteristic's barrier (Rev 14:4). Characteristic 3 anticipates: permanent non-defilement of the corporate community — "they shall not defile themselves anymore" (Eze 37:23); the holy city from which no defilement is admitted (Isa 52:1); the covenant formula permanently restored ("they shall be my people, and I will be their God"). Characteristic 4 anticipates: a community in which no unclean spirit finds habitation; the comprehensive eschatological defeat of all adversarial spiritual powers. The cluster's unified eschatological vision: a community with unrestricted access to divine presence (Char 1), in permanent holiness (Char 2), in restored covenant relationship (Char 3), free from all adversarial spiritual defilement (Char 4). These four dimensions are the positive fullness toward which M10c's defilement domain is oriented.

findings.finding_value: T5 produces three inter-related formation findings. First, transformation is evidenced in both modes simultaneously (Luke 15:20-24 — the father's compassion produces condition-change in the son's standing AND orientation-change in his reception of identity). Second, the formative cycle is self-reinforcing: the after-state of compassion-received feeds back into the before-state of compassion-readiness in the future — the person who has received compassion becomes more capable of extending it. Third, compassion plays a dual role in the sanctification arc: it is simultaneously the character target being formed (the person becoming compassionate over time) and the motivational ground that makes the formative relationship survivable through failure and return. Matthew 18:27 introduces the most critical formative warning: received compassion can be forfeited by failure to extend it — compassion is not a permanently possessed gift but a participatory moral framework. Three distinct mechanisms of change operate across contexts: encounter/sudden (splanchnizō — the moment of being moved), covenantal-sustaining/gradual (chesed — the steady faithfulness over time), and participatory-ontological (2Pe 1:4 pattern — sharing in what God is). T5.7 is formally closed: no body deposit established. All four relationships between suffering and compassion are evidenced — suffering reveals, tests, deepens, and produces compassion.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-005: T5 produces the richest formation account of any characteristic in the review set. Five mechanisms of change are distinguished: encounter (specific relational event — Luk 1:28, Ruth 2:10), spirit-outp…
findings.finding_value: T5 produces the richest formation account of any characteristic in the review set. Five mechanisms of change are distinguished: encounter (specific relational event — Luk 1:28, Ruth 2:10), spirit-outpouring (Zec 12:10), word (Act 20:32 — grace operating through the proclaimed word), inference (Rom 8:32 — cognitive reasoning from the supreme grace-event to present assurance), and mediated-transformation (grace → tenderheartedness → forgiving — Eph 4:32, SD030). Five distinct mechanisms for a single characteristic is unique in the programme data. The creaturely recognition response (fear → mourning → prostration) is confirmed as a consistent transitional state in all grace-sequences across different evidential contexts — not incidental detail but structural feature. Suffering's relationship to grace is precisely distinguished: grace inhabits suffering rather than suffering producing grace (2Cor 12:9 — weakness as theatre of grace, not as generator of grace). The reversibility question (T5.1 P2) is the most significant gap: not fully resolved. The eschatological trajectory (T5.6) is evidenced through Eph 2:7 ("the immeasurable riches of his grace in the coming ages") and charitoō's perfect-passive form (completed state with continuing effect). T2.8 remains open; T5.7 is formally left open accordingly.

The strife-and-quarrel corpus (M02-F) is largely silent on positive eschatological trajectory — it describes the characteristic as a work of the flesh to be put away. The implicit trajectory is toward the elimination of strife, but the positive fullness beyond its absence is not described.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, strongly. (1) The Day-of-the-Lord material (Isa 2:9-17; 13:11) points toward eschatological completion. (2) 1Cor 15:43 — body sown in dishonor, raised in glory — is the eschatological resolution of CHAR-2 at the individual level. (3) Hab 2:16 — "utter shame will come upon your glory" — is directed eschatologically: God's cup of judgment will finally execute the complete reversal of all proud human standing.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The structural-dishonour mode (VCG-02) points toward its own eschatological resolution: 2Ti 2:20's vessel for dishonorable use is implicitly oriented toward the possibility of cleansing (2:21 context). Rom 9:21's potter-and-clay raises the deepest eschatological question: sovereign assignment of dishonour-standings as a condition of creaturely existence, and whether eschatological transformation re-assigns those standings.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — Rev 16:15 frames CHAR-4's proper functioning as oriented toward the moment of Christ's coming: the one who "stays awake, keeping his garments on" avoids the shame of exposure at that moment. The eschatological fullness is the state in which moral vigilance has been sustained and the shameful has been renounced throughout — so that at Christ's coming no exposure occurs. CHAR-4's eschatological trajectory is toward the full activation and correct calibration of the moral-evaluative conscience.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes. Act 4:11 (the rejected stone becoming the cornerstone) is the paradigmatic eschatological statement of CHAR-5's reversal. 1Cor 1:28 (God choosing the despised to nullify things that are) is the eschatological programme: the world's contempt-verdicts are being overturned, and this overturning will be completed in the eschaton. The present experience of CHAR-5 anticipates its final reversal — shame from contempt is a temporary condition oriented toward the vindicating re-worth-assignment of God.
